item.title: Drone Strikes Across Sudan Kill More Than 100 People
item.description: A wave of drone strikes targeting war-torn Sudan’s army-held capital Khartoum and two western areas controlled by paramilitary forces has killed more than 100 people since Sunday, according to residents, medical workers and paramilitary sources. The deadliest drone strike hit near a market on Sunday evening in Al-Dibab town in the southwestern state of West Kordofan, which is controlled by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) that have been at war with Sudan’s military since April 2023. Residents and medical workers said a drone struck a transport hub where villagers had gathered after a market day to find rides home, killing 80 people. Ahmed Abakar Wadi, a resident who helped bury victims, told AFP at least 50 bodies were recovered at the scene, including that of his brother. Another 47 wounded people were taken to the nearby town of Al-Mujlad where 30 later died from their injuries, according to a medical source. “The drone struck once, and then came back 10 minutes later and struck again,” Wadi told AFP. The RSF’s self-declared administration, known as Tasis, and the Sudanese rights group Emergency Lawyers accused the army of carrying out the attack. The military has not commented. The strike was one of the deadliest single attacks in Kordofan, an oil-rich region linking western and eastern Sudan where the army and the RSF have been battling for territory. Dams targeted This screen grab made from the UGC footage obtained on October 12, 2026 shows people inspecting the site of an airstrike in the mining area of Jabal al-Uqaydat, in Sudan. AFP Hours later, early on Monday, another drone attack hit the RSF stronghold of Nyala, the capital of South Darfur. Medical and RSF sources said 17 people, including seven RSF officers, were killed and 23 wounded when a drone struck the city centre and destroyed two homes. On Monday morning, violence also reached the capital Khartoum, where a drone strike hit a house in a neighbourhood east of Khartoum airport, killing four people, including three children aged between two and six, according to a medical source. An army official said Sudanese air defences had intercepted drones launched by the RSF that were targeting the airport and nearby areas. In eastern Sudan, a military source said on Sunday that air defences also intercepted several RSF drones targeting the Atbara and Setit dams in Gadaref state, about 420 kilometres east of Khartoum. There is no definitive toll for Sudan’s conflict, but aid workers estimate it has killed more than 200,000 people and created what aid agencies describe as the world’s largest hunger and displacement crisis. More than 1,100 people were killed in drone attacks across Sudan during the first half of this year alone, according to the United Nations. item.content:encoded: A wave of drone strikes targeting war-torn Sudan’s army-held capital Khartoum and two western areas controlled by paramilitary forces has killed more than 100 people since Sunday, according to residents, medical workers and paramilitary sources. The deadliest drone strike hit near a market on Sunday evening in Al-Dibab town in the southwestern state of West Kordofan, which is controlled by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) that have been at war with Sudan’s military since April 2023. Residents and medical workers said a drone struck a transport hub where villagers had gathered after a market day to find rides home, killing 80 people. Ahmed Abakar Wadi, a resident who helped bury victims, told AFP at least 50 bodies were recovered at the scene, including that of his brother. Another 47 wounded people were taken to the nearby town of Al-Mujlad where 30 later died from their injuries, according to a medical source. “The drone struck once, and then came back 10 minutes later and struck again,” Wadi told AFP. The RSF’s self-declared administration, known as Tasis, and the Sudanese rights group Emergency Lawyers accused the army of carrying out the attack. The military has not commented. The strike was one of the deadliest single attacks in Kordofan, an oil-rich region linking western and eastern Sudan where the army and the RSF have been battling for territory. Dams targeted This screen grab made from the UGC footage obtained on October 12, 2026 shows people inspecting the site of an airstrike in the mining area of Jabal al-Uqaydat, in Sudan. AFP Hours later, early on Monday, another drone attack hit the RSF stronghold of Nyala, the capital of South Darfur. Medical and RSF sources said 17 people, including seven RSF officers, were killed and 23 wounded when a drone struck the city centre and destroyed two homes. On Monday morning, violence also reached the capital Khartoum, where a drone strike hit a house in a neighbourhood east of Khartoum airport, killing four people, including three children aged between two and six, according to a medical source. An army official said Sudanese air defences had intercepted drones launched by the RSF that were targeting the airport and nearby areas. In eastern Sudan, a military source said on Sunday that air defences also intercepted several RSF drones targeting the Atbara and Setit dams in Gadaref state, about 420 kilometres east of Khartoum. There is no definitive toll for Sudan’s conflict, but aid workers estimate it has killed more than 200,000 people and created what aid agencies describe as the world’s largest hunger and displacement crisis. More than 1,100 people were killed in drone attacks across Sudan during the first half of this year alone, according to the United Nations. Kordofan — home to oil deposits and the RSF’s most powerful paramilitary allies — has come under repeated drone attacks in recent months as the army seeks to roll back RSF gains made last year after the paramilitary group consolidated control over much of Darfur. On Friday, a drone strike on a cattle market in Nyala, Sudan’s second-largest city and the seat of the RSF’s self-declared administration, killed 30 people and injured 47 others, according to a medical source. item.title: UIL approves girls flag football pilot program, set to launch in 2028-29
item.description: A large sign announces the Texas State Championship competition in Girls Flag Football along the sidelines of one of the playing fields. The girls high school flag football championship tournament was held at the University of North Texas DATCU Stadium in Denton on June 13, 2026. (Steve Hamm/The Dallas Morning News) Girls flag football is one step closer to becoming a UIL-sanctioned sport. The UIL legislative council approved a proposal to begin a girls flag football pilot program, beginning in the 2028-29 school year with no more than two conferences. The proposal needs final approval from the Texas Commissioner of Education. As of fall 2027, 25 states will have sanctioned girls flag football. A superintendent survey conducted by the UIL this fall found that 52% of Class 6A and 5A superintendents support the adoption of flag football as a sanctioned sport. The survey also found that 165 schools currently offer the sport. The Houston Texans and the Dallas Cowboys have been advocating for the addition of girls flag football as a sanctioned UIL sport for multiple years. Flag football is quickly growing across the country at all levels. The NCAA added flag football to its Emerging Sports for Women program in January, which gives the sport a pathway to become an NCAA-sanctioned activity. Sports like rowing, beach volleyball and water polo have previously gone through the program and are now NCAA-championship sports. Our Lady of the Lake launched a women's flag football program this school year, becoming the first San Antonio area university to do so. The NAIA is set to name a flag football national champion for the first time in spring 2027. Flag football, both men's and women's, is also set to make its Olympics debut in 2028. Carrollton Newman Smith's Leanna Garcia (10), right with ball, attempts to maneuver away from Rockwall Heath defender Laurelea Carlyle (8) as she attempts to remove her flag as Heath defenders Reece Bouchard (12), Olivia Richard (6) and Leah Wilson (13) close in on the play during second half action. Heath won, 27-0 on Day 1 of the girls high school flag football championship tournament which was held at the University of North Texas DATCU Stadium in Denton on June 13, 2026. (Steve Hamm/The Dallas Morning News) According to the Houston Chronicle's Jon Poorman, participation in the Texans and Cowboys' programs is expected to reach more than 270 schools and around 6,000 athletes by 2027. The two NFL teams hosted the first girls flag football state championship at DATCU Stadium on the University of North Texas campus from June 13-14, four years after piloting their own programs. Rockwall-Heath took down Houston Memorial, 25-6, for the state title. A superintendent survey conducted by the UIL this fall found that 52% of Class 6A and 5A superintendents support the adoption of flag football as a sanctioned sport. The survey also found that 165 schools currently offer the sport. The Houston Texans and the Dallas Cowboys have been advocating for the addition of girls flag football as a sanctioned UIL sport for multiple years. The NCAA added flag football to its Emerging Sports for Women program in January, which gives the sport a pathway to become an NCAA-sanctioned activity. The NAIA is set to name a flag football national champion for the first time in spring 2027. Flag football, both men's and women's, is also set to make its Olympics debut in 2028. Carrollton Newman Smith's Leanna Garcia (10), right with ball, attempts to maneuver away from Rockwall Heath defender Laurelea Carlyle (8) as she attempts to remove her flag as Heath defenders Reece Bouchard (12), Olivia Richard (6) and Leah Wilson (13) close in on the play during second half action. Heath won, 27-0 on Day 1 of the girls high school flag football championship tournament which was held at the University of North Texas DATCU Stadium in Denton on June 13, 2026. (Steve Hamm/The Dallas Morning News) According to the Houston Chronicle's Jon Poorman, participation in the Texans and Cowboys' programs is expected to reach more than 270 schools and around 6,000 athletes by 2027. Monday's UIL proposal did not specify where girls flag football would fall into the academic calendar, and the timing for the flag football season varies across the country. Some states that have already sanctioned girls flag football, like Georgia, have their seasons in the fall. This year's Georgia girls high school flag football championships will be held on Dec. 8 at Atlanta's Mercedes-Benz Stadium. New York's flag football season is held in the spring. item.title: A Japanese Spacecraft Aims to Bring Back a Bit of a Martian Moon
item.description: The mission, which launched on Monday, is headed to Phobos, the larger of the two moons of Mars. It could carry back the first samples from the Martian system.

item.title: Fantasy Football Impact: Josh Jacobs' Status For Week 7 Is To Be Determined
item.description: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs (8) stiff-arms Cincinnati Bengals cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt (29) on Sunday, October 12, 2025, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wis. The Packers won the game, 27-18. Tork Mason/USA TODAY NETWORK-Wisconsin | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect After a six-week-long wait, fantasy football owners are chomping at the bit to see Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs back on the field and get him back in their lineups. However, there is a chance that they could have to wait beyond Week 7. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said that he will get a full week of practice, but he is not a lock to play next week after missing so much time. LaFleur said he's been training, but his status is still to be determined: "We feel like he's in a pretty good spot. He's been training, but he's missed the exposure to football." Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Josh Jacobs will practice on Wednesday and get a full week of work but TBD on whether he'll play on Sunday at Detroit. "We feel like he's in a pretty good spot. He's been training, but he's missed the exposure to football." - Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) October 19, 2026 Fantasy Impact RB Josh Jacobs, Green Bay Packers We expect Jacobs to be out there in Week 7. It would be a shock if they held him out for a week to get in shape. If he's been training, he should be in good enough shape to get on the field. Jacobs has shown us nothing in his career on the field that would lead us to believe that he has been sitting on his coach eating Cheese Doodles and not keeping in shape for a return. However, there is a chance that he could take a week to ramp up in a more split workload. He won't necessarily be on a snap count, but he also probably won't see a full bell-cow workload. While we expect him to be in shape, being in shape and handling a near-every-down role in an NFL game are very different. If you have Jacobs and he's active, you can safely start him this week. The other running backs in Green Bay have been horrible, and they could need Jacobs out there to defeat the Detroit Lions in Week 7. RB MarShawn Lloyd, Green Bay Packers After a mostly disastrous six weeks, you can now drop all those useless Packers' backup running backs. You can safely cut Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson. There is no reason to hold them and clog up a roster spot because we've already seen how they look if Jacobs goes down, and it's not good. It's certainly not worth holding them as handcuffs just in case. item.title: Serie A | Parma 0-3 Torino: Simeone double spoils Gilardino’s Tardini bow
item.description: Serie A | Parma 0-3 Torino: Simeone double spoils Gilardino’s Tardini bow Giovanni Simeone struck twice and Che Adams headed in as Torino spoiled Alberto Gilardino’s first home game in charge of Parma with a 3-0 win at the Tardini. Gilardino’s Parma went into the game on four points after a 3-0 defeat at Inter, and were without Hans Nicolussi Caviglia, Pontus Almqvist and Elphege, who had surgery for appendicitis. Adrián Bernabé returned to the midfield, with Giovanni Fabbian also starting. Ignazio Abate’s Torino had beaten Udinese last time out but were missing Niccolò Fortini and Emirhan Ilkhan. Ardian Ismajli came into the defence in place of Ricardo Rodríguez. Torino made a fast start. Adams had a volley blocked inside the opening minute and Saúl Coco headed off target from the resulting corner. They went ahead on four minutes, when Rafik Belghali lofted a cross into the box and Simeone met it with a left-footed finish into the top corner. Pietro Comuzzo headed wide from close range before Torino doubled their lead on 24 minutes. Simeone’s shot was blocked and Adams reacted first to nod home the rebound, with the goal surviving a VAR check for offside. Parma did respond. Lucas Perri made a superb diving save to keep out David Romero, then gathered headers from Diego Carlos and Fabbian. Enrico Delprato should have pulled one back just before the break, but steered wide from inside the six-yard box. PARMA, ITALY – OCTOBER 19: Nikola Vlasic of Torino FC runs with the ball during the Serie A match between Parma Calcio and Torino FC at Stadio Ennio Tardini on October 19, 2026 in Parma, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images) Parma pile on the pressure but Torino put the game to bed Gilardino made a double change at half-time, bringing on Dominik Drobnič and Simone Lontani. El Bilal Touré headed narrowly wide, Lontani fired over, and Perri saved from Bernabé and Mariano Troilo. Sascha Britschgi was booked for diving. Romero curled just past the far post before Torino put the game to bed on 69 minutes. Simeone collected Belghali’s headed pass and unleashed a fierce strike from distance into the top corner. Substitute Matija Frigan thought he had pulled one back from Djibril Diallo’s pass, but VAR ruled it out for offside. Perri then comfortably held his effort after a solo run late on. Parma 0-3 Torino Simeone 4, 69 (T), Adams 24 (T)

Pietro Comuzzo headed wide from close range before Torino doubled their lead on 24 minutes. Simeone’s shot was blocked and Adams reacted first to nod home the rebound, with the goal surviving a VAR check for offside. Parma did respond. Lucas Perri made a superb diving save to keep out David Romero, then gathered headers from Diego Carlos and Fabbian. Enrico Delprato should have pulled one back just before the break, but steered wide from inside the six-yard box. PARMA, ITALY – OCTOBER 19: Nikola Vlasic of Torino FC runs with the ball during the Serie A match between Parma Calcio and Torino FC at Stadio Ennio Tardini on October 19, 2026 in Parma, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images) Parma pile on the pressure but Torino put the game to bed Gilardino made a double change at half-time, bringing on Dominik Drobnič and Simone Lontani. El Bilal Touré headed narrowly wide, Lontani fired over, and Perri saved from Bernabé and Mariano Troilo. Sascha Britschgi was booked for diving. Romero curled just past the far post before Torino put the game to bed on 69 minutes. Simeone collected Belghali’s headed pass and unleashed a fierce strike from distance into the top corner. Substitute Matija Frigan thought he had pulled one back from Djibril Diallo’s pass, but VAR ruled it out for offside. Perri then comfortably held his effort after a solo run late on. Parma 0-3 Torino Simeone 4, 69 (T), Adams 24 (T)

item.title: Who's Field Hockey Player of the Week, presented by White Plains Hospital?
item.description: Since the beginning of fall season, readers have selected the lohud Field Hockey Player of the Week, sponsored by White Plains Hospital. Last week's winner was Ava Galati, a Clarkstown South senior, who excelled at midfield and on offensive and defensive corners over two games, including during a win over Suffern. She joined earlier winners Alina Cavajani of Panas, Alexa Butler of Clarkstown, Taylor Stillwaggon of Mahopac, Sophia Gac of Valhalla and Lila Walsh of North Rockland. This week, coaches have nominated seven athletes for their Oct. 12-18 play. Their accomplishments are noted below. The poll will close at 3 p.m. Wednesday. Micalyn Kelly, White Plains The senior midfielder, who leads her team in assists with 14 and has been a consistent force on offense, picked up three assists in a 7-1 win over Rye Neck and scored in the Tigers' 4-1 win over Fox Lane. Aimee Kovacs, Somers The Tuskers senior netminder recorded her ninth and 10th shutouts of the season last week. She stopped four shots in a 1-0 win over Scarsdale and earlier in the week, on Somers Senior Night, she shut down Arlington, making nine saves in a 2-0 Tusker win. Kayleigh Pontillo, Mahopac The senior forward scored both the game-tying and overtime game-winning goal in a 3-2 win over Pelham. With the OT winner, Pontillo dribbled past two Pelicans defensemen and scored after going in one-on-one on the Pelham goalie. Millie Nemser, Rye Country Day The junior forward set a Rye Country Day School record by recording two hat tricks in a single week. She had three goals in a 4-1 win over St. Luke's before putting another three in in a 5-2 win over Holy Child. Leah Schaedler, Nanuet The senior midfielder was a force on offense last week, scoring four goals and recording an assist, She scored twice in the Golden Knights/ 7-0 win over Byram Hills, scored in a 4-3 loss to Hastings, registered the assist in a 4-2 win over Croton/Hen Hud and scored in a 3-1 loss to Pawling. Elizabeth Torres, Suffern Coming off a week in which she scored twice, including netting an overtime game-winner, the senior midfielder again scored twice and added two assists in a 7-1 win over Nyack. The following day, she returned to overtime heroics, scoring with five seconds left in OT as the Mounties edged Pleasantville 2-1. Luca Vecchiariello, Pleasantville The senior is an upper defenseman, whose role is critical in stopping opponents' initial advances down the field. She excelled doing that in a 2-1 win over Ursuline. Vecchiariello made multiple block tackles, stole the ball multiple times and, dodging opponents, helped create multiple offensive chances for the Panthers. Nancy Haggerty covers sports for The Journal News/lohud . This article originally appeared on Rockland/Westchester Journal News: Who's Field Hockey Player of the Week, presented by White Plains Hospital?

item.title: Ronaldo given 30-day suspension and £215 fine by Portuguese FA
item.description: Ronaldo has scored 146 goals in 234 Portugal appearances [Getty Images] Cristiano Ronaldo has been given a 30-day suspension and fined 255 euros (£215) by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after leaving his country's international camp last month. The 41-year-old captain walked out of Portugal's Nations League squad in September after being an unused substitute against Norway and then finding out he would not start against Denmark on 1 October. Ronaldo said in a lengthy statement he had left because Portugal coach Jorge Jesus twice "broke his word", accusing him of an "absolute breach of trust". The Al-Nassr forward's suspension takes effect from the day of the Denmark match, meaning he has already served 19 days of his ban and will complete it by the end of the month. The FPF disciplinary committee said it took into account "the remorse shown" by Ronaldo in his statement. He accepted accountability and apologised to his team-mates and fans for his actions, before adding he deserved to be punished. Portugal boss Jesus denied making any agreement with Ronaldo but has left the door open for his return. Pedro Proenca, president of the FPF, told Portuguese outlet Record there is a "strong desire" to have Ronaldo back with the national team once the matter is resolved. The five-time Ballon d'Or winner has scored 146 goals in 234 Portugal appearances - both men's world records - helping them win Euro 2016 and the two Nations League titles. He joined Saudi Arabian side Al-Nassr in December 2022 on a reported annual salary of £177m and signed a contract extension last year. Ronaldo wants Portugal 'punishment' but not retiring A nation divided as Ronaldo left with big decision on Portugal future Ronaldo leaves Portugal camp after coach denies rift

item.title: Building Lionesses 2.0 - Wiegman's new challenge awaits
item.description: Sarina Wiegman has won the past three Women's European Championships - with the Netherlands in 2017 and England in 2022 and 2025 [Getty Images] When Sarina Wiegman took the reins as England manager in September 2021, she declared she had "come to bring the next level". Winner of the 2017 Women's Euros with her own Netherlands and runner-up at the subsequent World Cup in 2019, she certainly had the pedigree, but could she deliver on her promises? Five years on, Wiegman has pocketed two more European Championships and acquired another silver medal on the global stage. Not only that, but the success of her Lionesses exploded the women's game in this country, taking it not just to a new level, but to previously unthinkable heights. And yet on the day Wiegman extends her deal until after the Euros in 2029, her newest challenge could be her hardest yet. England manager Wiegman signs contract extension Why must England evolve? [BBC] Wiegman's successful England teams have been built on a core group of players from an outstanding generation - but a few cracks have appeared this year. Seven of the team that started against world champions Spain in June also played in the Euro 2022 final against Germany - and their 4-0 defeat in Mallorca laid bare the gap England must bridge to the world's best. That result also consigned England to two rounds of play-offs to reach next summer's World Cup. Beating Greece this month navigated the first of those, with games against Ukraine, who they have beaten twice already in 2026, to come before Christmas. Nevertheless, finding successors to those who have spearheaded the success will not be straightforward. Defensive stalwarts Lucy Bronze and Alex Greenwood will be 37 and 36 respectively by Euro 2029, while Leah Williamson and Keira Walsh will be 32. Other key players such as Alessia Russo and Georgia Stanway will also have turned 30, far from past their best, but still a consideration. "We have to continue the evolution of the Lionesses," record goalscorer Ellen White told the Women's Football Weekly podcast. "We can't stay stagnant or keep trying to win in the same ways all the time." Former England goalkeeper Rachel Brown-Finnis thinks one of Wiegman's strengths as a manager is her willingness to give young players a chance. "She's not afraid of bringing in players who have never been capped before," Brown-Finnis told BBC Radio 5 Live. "Wiegman is looking right across the spectrum and asking who's on form, who can add to my squad, who can fill a position or a couple of different positions?" Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live's Monday Night Club, former Lionesses captain Steph Houghton said: "You can see Wiegman is trying to change a few things. The last camp she brought on Lexi Potter for her debut and she is now starting regularly for Chelsea. As a young player you need that to thrive in this environment. "She is seeing the progress of young players coming through to press those who have been in the squad for a long time."
item.content:encoded: Sarina Wiegman has won the past three Women's European Championships - with the Netherlands in 2017 and England in 2022 and 2025 [Getty Images] When Sarina Wiegman took the reins as England manager in September 2021, she declared she had "come to bring the next level". Winner of the 2017 Women's Euros with her own Netherlands and runner-up at the subsequent World Cup in 2019, she certainly had the pedigree, but could she deliver on her promises? Five years on, Wiegman has pocketed two more European Championships and acquired another silver medal on the global stage. Not only that, but the success of her Lionesses exploded the women's game in this country, taking it not just to a new level, but to previously unthinkable heights. And yet on the day Wiegman extends her deal until after the Euros in 2029, her newest challenge could be her hardest yet. England manager Wiegman signs contract extension Why must England evolve? [BBC] Wiegman's successful England teams have been built on a core group of players from an outstanding generation - but a few cracks have appeared this year. Seven of the team that started against world champions Spain in June also played in the Euro 2022 final against Germany - and their 4-0 defeat in Mallorca laid bare the gap England must bridge to the world's best. That result also consigned England to two rounds of play-offs to reach next summer's World Cup. Beating Greece this month navigated the first of those, with games against Ukraine, who they have beaten twice already in 2026, to come before Christmas. Nevertheless, finding successors to those who have spearheaded the success will not be straightforward. Defensive stalwarts Lucy Bronze and Alex Greenwood will be 37 and 36 respectively by Euro 2029, while Leah Williamson and Keira Walsh will be 32. Other key players such as Alessia Russo and Georgia Stanway will also have turned 30, far from past their best, but still a consideration. "We have to continue the evolution of the Lionesses," record goalscorer Ellen White told the Women's Football Weekly podcast. "We can't stay stagnant or keep trying to win in the same ways all the time." Former England goalkeeper Rachel Brown-Finnis thinks one of Wiegman's strengths as a manager is her willingness to give young players a chance. "She's not afraid of bringing in players who have never been capped before," Brown-Finnis told BBC Radio 5 Live. "Wiegman is looking right across the spectrum and asking who's on form, who can add to my squad, who can fill a position or a couple of different positions?" Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live's Monday Night Club, former Lionesses captain Steph Houghton said: "You can see Wiegman is trying to change a few things. The last camp she brought on Lexi Potter for her debut and she is now starting regularly for Chelsea. As a young player you need that to thrive in this environment. "She is seeing the progress of young players coming through to press those who have been in the squad for a long time." Greek takeaways: What did we learn from Lionesses' win? Who is ready to step up? It is not as though Wiegman has ignored squad regeneration. During her time in charge, she has handed debuts to 24 players, but only Lauren James, Hannah Hampton and Lucia Kendall have become established starters. Those games against Greece offered a clue to her next steps. In Crete, Manchester City's Laura Blindkilde Brown, 23, showed glimpses of her ball-playing ability, while in the second leg 20-year-old Chelsea academy graduate Potter impressed in midfield. London City's Freya Godfrey, 21, and talented 18-year-old Erica Meg Parkinson also got their first caps as Wiegman scrutinised her options. Figures earlier this season showed the number of homegrown starters has been dropping in the Women's Super League (WSL) over the past four campaigns, with the league's growing prestige attracting more foreign stars. The Football Association (FA) chief football officer Dan Ashworth said Wiegman has helped bring "a golden age for women's football in this country". To prolong it, she will need to keep producing fruit from increasingly arid ground. 'Alarming' - does WSL have a homegrown problem? Could Potter be England's next breakthrough star? Why is it different now? Prior to Wiegman's appointment, England women had performed well at major tournaments - finishing third at the World Cup in 2015 and fourth in 2019 - but winning Euro 2022 was something new. WSL attendances rocketed, media coverage surged and clubs amplified their women's teams. However, four years on, there is evidence to suggest interest has plateaued. Initial crowd figures for the 2026-27 season are down on previous campaigns, while only 18,587 fans watched England beat Greece 5-0 at King Power Stadium, nearly 10,000 fewer than qualifiers at Nottingham Forest's City Ground and Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium this year. With so much competition, Lionesses success is crucial for sustaining momentum in the women's game - but expectations are higher now. A fanbase was born from success and has become accustomed to it. Will they tolerate anything less than finals and trophies? After all, Spain, Japan and hosts Brazil are among the many nations that look poised to have a significant say at the World Cup next summer. Only four of the top 10 nations in Fifa's world rankings have female managers (Spain, USA and Canada), with Wiegman the longest serving. If she sees out her contract, only Hope Powell (1998-2013) and Martin Reagan (1979-90), will have been England head coach for longer. As she signed her new contract, she said she "could not think of a better job in world football". It is hard to think of many who have done a better job than Wiegman has already accomplished. Committing to three more years means her legacy may now be defined by what she achieves next. Head here to get involved

item.title: Maresca surpasses Guardiola as City continue perfect league start
item.description: Maresca surpasses Guardiola as City continue perfect league start Enzo Maresca has made Premier League history at Manchester City , becoming the first manager to win his opening seven league games in charge of a club. City maintained their perfect start with Saturday’s 3-2 victory over Ipswich Town, taking their points tally to 21 in 21 possible. Maresca’s side have also claimed wins over Bournemouth , Crystal Palace, Coventry City, Manchester United, Sunderland and Liverpool during their remarkable run. Maresca has surpassed the previous benchmark of six consecutive wins set by Pep Guardiola at City, Carlo Ancelotti at Chelsea and Ole Gunnar Solskjær at Manchester United. City have scored 19 goals and conceded six during their opening seven league games, underlining their strength at both ends of the pitch. When it comes to best start to a season, Chelsea set the benchmark with nine straight wins to open the 2005-06 season, while Liverpool came close in 2019-20, winning their first eight matches. Although defeats to Arsenal in the Community Shield and Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League have interrupted their progress elsewhere, Maresca’s domestic start has put City in a strong position early in the season.

item.title: 🔥 Simeone inspires Torino: stunning brace, Parma beaten again ‼
item.description: 🔥 Simeone inspires Torino: stunning brace, Parma beaten again ‼ Torino claim a commanding win at the Tardini, beating Parma 3-0 to secure their second consecutive victory. Watch all of Serie BKT live with LaB Channel on OneFootball: subscribe for just €9.99 a month! The Granata take control straight away: in the 4th minute, Simeone volleys home Belghali’s assist to finish off a superb counterattack, before Che Adams heads in the second following another effort from the Argentine. After the break, Parma try to raise the tempo and create several chances, but are punished again during their best spell: in the 69th minute, Simeone picks up the ball on the edge of the box and unleashes a thunderous right-footed strike into the top corner , undoubtedly the best goal of this Monday, to make it three. Frigan also finds the net late on, only for VAR to rule it out for offside. The headlines belong to Giovanni Simeone , who scores his first brace in a Torino shirt and nets more than once in a match for the first time in four and a half years: his last multiple-goal haul was a hat-trick in Verona’s 3-1 win over Venezia. An excellent display from Abate ’s men, who are clinical in front of goal and withstand the hosts’ response. For Gilardino’s Parma , meanwhile, it is another defeat, with fans voicing their displeasure both during and after the match. Parma remain second from bottom, with another worrying statistic unchanged: they still have Serie A’s worst attack . This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: African wonderkid closing in on joining Andoni Iraola's Liverpool first-team
item.description: African wonderkid closing in on joining Andoni Iraola's Liverpool first-team Andoni Iraola's first-team could soon be bolstered by an exciting African wonderkid. The Spaniard has been a breath of fresh air since his arrival. Under Arne Slot, Liverpool have lost their identity. The Dutchman may be a good coach but he was simply not the right fit for Liverpool. Slot showed what he was capable of during his first year in charge. However, he also showed what he was not capable of in his second season in charge. When he had to work with a strong squad, and players who had already achieved or come close to fulfiling their potential, Slot flourished. However, when he was forced to develop players, work with youngsters and promote from the academy, he faltered. Slot just didn't seem to be that type of manager. He was a farcry from Jurgen Klopp, who relished working with youngsters. Andoni Iraola's exciting young generation at Liverpool From the get-go Iraola has proven he is different. In pre-season, he was not afraid of throwing a 16-year-old in Joshua Abe at the deep-end. He also gave Ifeanyi Ndukwe an increased playing time, and opted to promote Lewis Koumas after he recognised the Welshman was the perfect fit for his philosophy. Under Iraola, the Reds youngsters are now finally getting chances. Trey Nyoni has had the opportunity to establish himself as a key midfielder. Koumas has become a great source of energy off the bench. And Rio Ngumoha is slowly getting better and better on the right-wing. Iraola is proving that he has that Klopp touch about him. He is able to get the maximum out of all of his players and he is willing to reward younger players the chance to prove themselves. Mor Talla Ndiaye is closing in on the first-team At the same time, Iraola is also having to contend with injury problems. Right now, Jeremie Frimpong has a knock, and Dominik Szoboszlai is also out injured. Injuries usually means an opportunity for someone else who is catching the eye at academy level to be promoted. And one of those players who is now really pushing in earning a promotion to the senior squad is Mor Talla Ndiaye. The Senegalese U17 international has been a revelation since he arrived in the January window earlier this year. He is a commanding and extremely composed defender. Ndiaye recently scored a 92nd minute winner for Liverpool's U21 side against West Brom. He is getting better and better, and it's only a matter of time until Iraola calls him up for the first-team. It very much feels like Ndiaye is on the verge of joining the senior squad.

item.title: Florida is No. 1 again. Last season explains why the Gators still have something to prove
item.description: Florida is No. 1 again. Last season explains why the Gators still have something to prove originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Florida opens the 2026-27 men’s college basketball season atop the AP Top 25, with 47 of 59 first-place votes. The ranking puts the Gators back in familiar territory after their 2025 national championship, but it also brings an uncomfortable recent memory: last season began with Florida at No. 3, then saw the Gators fall out of the poll by early January. They recovered to win the SEC regular-season title, only to lose to Iowa as a No. 1 seed in the second round of the NCAA Tournament. That sharp turn makes this preseason ranking more than a compliment. It is a test of whether Florida can carry lofty expectations through the long middle of the season. The Gators are No. 1 in the men's basketball preseason AP Poll 🏀 https://t.co/5ft3dT7FMH — ESPN (@espn) October 19, 2026 The No. 1 ranking comes with a built-in reminder The Gators have a compelling case. Thomas Haugh, Alex Condon and Rueben Chinyelu are back from the title team, while Denzel Aberdeen returns after spending last season at Kentucky. That gives coach Todd Golden a core that has experienced the biggest stage and the frustration of a season that ended short of its goal. Florida’s returning group is a real advantage in a sport where rosters can change dramatically from one year to the next. But last season showed that experience alone does not make a team immune to a rough stretch. The Gators will need to turn their familiarity with each other into steadier play when the schedule gets difficult. MORE : Trey Kaufman-Renn signs with Kansas after starring at Purdue Duke and Illinois are close enough to make this a race Duke received 10 first-place votes and sits at No. 2. Illinois is No. 3 after receiving the other two. Florida has a strong lead in the vote, but the poll offers no guarantees once the games begin. UConn and Arizona round out the top five, giving the preseason ranking a crowded championship conversation from the start. Golden has said the program should expect to compete at this level. That is the mindset of a team that has won a title. The challenge is matching that confidence with the consistency Florida lacked last winter. The No. 1 spot is a headline today; keeping the Gators there will take months of work. item.content:encoded: Florida is No. 1 again. Last season explains why the Gators still have something to prove originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Florida opens the 2026-27 men’s college basketball season atop the AP Top 25, with 47 of 59 first-place votes. The ranking puts the Gators back in familiar territory after their 2025 national championship, but it also brings an uncomfortable recent memory: last season began with Florida at No. 3, then saw the Gators fall out of the poll by early January. They recovered to win the SEC regular-season title, only to lose to Iowa as a No. 1 seed in the second round of the NCAA Tournament. That sharp turn makes this preseason ranking more than a compliment. It is a test of whether Florida can carry lofty expectations through the long middle of the season. The Gators are No. 1 in the men's basketball preseason AP Poll 🏀 https://t.co/5ft3dT7FMH — ESPN (@espn) October 19, 2026 The No. 1 ranking comes with a built-in reminder The Gators have a compelling case. Thomas Haugh, Alex Condon and Rueben Chinyelu are back from the title team, while Denzel Aberdeen returns after spending last season at Kentucky. That gives coach Todd Golden a core that has experienced the biggest stage and the frustration of a season that ended short of its goal. Florida’s returning group is a real advantage in a sport where rosters can change dramatically from one year to the next. But last season showed that experience alone does not make a team immune to a rough stretch. The Gators will need to turn their familiarity with each other into steadier play when the schedule gets difficult. MORE : Trey Kaufman-Renn signs with Kansas after starring at Purdue Duke and Illinois are close enough to make this a race Duke received 10 first-place votes and sits at No. 2. Illinois is No. 3 after receiving the other two. Florida has a strong lead in the vote, but the poll offers no guarantees once the games begin. UConn and Arizona round out the top five, giving the preseason ranking a crowded championship conversation from the start. Golden has said the program should expect to compete at this level. That is the mindset of a team that has won a title. The challenge is matching that confidence with the consistency Florida lacked last winter. The No. 1 spot is a headline today; keeping the Gators there will take months of work. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo receives 30-day suspension and £215 fine over Portugal walkout
item.description: Disciplinary council upholds charge against 41-year-old Fifa suspends Egypt’s Hossam Hassan and Mostafa Ziko Cristiano Ronaldo has been suspended for 30 days by the Portuguese ⁠FA after leaving the national team camp following a rift with the coach, ⁠Jorge Jesus, over ⁠his role in the side. The federation’s disciplinary council said it had upheld the charge against ⁠the 41-year-old forward in full and imposed a fine of €255 (£215). Ronaldo left Portugal’s base in ⁠Copenhagen before their Nations League match against Denmark earlier this month, having accused ‌Jesus of twice ‌breaking his word about his role after he was an ‌unused substitute against Norway. Jesus denied making any agreement with Ronaldo but left the door open for his return after Portugal’s 2-1 win. Continue reading...

item.title: Nic Claxton Out Two Weeks Leaves Bulls With Thin Frontcourt
item.description: Matt Marton-Imagn Images The Chicago Bulls are starting their season without their big man. Nic Claxton will miss at least the first two weeks of the regular season due to a hamstring injury suffered in the preseason. This is a major hit for a team that needs size. Coach Tiago Splitter confirmed the timeline on Monday after the medical staff re-evaluated the center this week. Splitter knows fans want a hard date. He told the media that he cannot give one. “This is not a science,” Splitter said. “I wish I could tell you guys, ‘Hey, 13 (days) left and then he’s going to play.’ It’s not like that. Everybody’s different. Everybody reacts to treatment different. Everybody reacts to practice different.”. The coach tried to be clear about the average recovery time. “On average, he should be back in two weeks. But that’s all I can do.”. Smith Steps Into the Starting Role Jalen Smith is the guy who has to fill the gap right now. He will start in the lineup while Claxton sits on the bench. Smith started most of the Bulls’ preseason games and should keep that role for the opener. This sets up a solid workload for him to open the season. The team opens Wednesday against the Raptors in Toronto. Smith has to be ready to lead the defense immediately. There is no time to warm up. The injury situation is not just about Claxton. Zach Collins is also sidelined by a quadriceps injury. Collins might return for Wednesday’s opener after practicing without limitations in Monday’s short session. According to the Chicago Tribune , Collins has not received clearance to play Wednesday. Collins was not restricted in Monday’s practice, which sets him up to be available for the game. The Bulls are hoping for a quick return, but the frontcourt is thin. Rebuild Patience Tested Early The Chicago Tribune reports the Bulls expect Claxton to be ready by the first week of November. That is a long wait for a team trying to find its footing. The team cannot play double-big lineups until everyone is healthy. Splitter had shown interest in those lineups because of the team’s personnel. Claxton will be re-evaluated in two weeks. Two days after reports surfaced that he was ramping up activity, Splitter confirmed the extended absence. K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports that Claxton will be re-evaluated in two weeks.

item.title: Star Wars Battlefront 3: Bungie Rumored as New Developer
item.description: There's a new and potentially exciting disturbance in the Force: Disney reportedly wants a new Star Wars Battlefront game, and it's eyeing two potential developers to tackle the project. One of those choices is unsurprising, while the other is supposedly Halo, Destiny, and Marathon studio Bungie. If true, long-suffering Star Wars shooter fans might finally get the Battlefront 3 they've wanted for more than 20 years.

item.title: Marion Harding boys win a championship, plus more league XC results
item.description: Marion Harding was pointing to Oct. 17 all season. The Presidents felt they could win a Mid Ohio Athletic Conference boys cross country championship on their own course. "Honestly we’ve raced really good this season," Marion Harding coach Bob Peters said. "We made it a point to win the conference this year. I felt like we were racing well against the conference throughout the year when we saw somebody. The guys wanted this. They came in locked-in on this meet." As they envisioned, the Presidents won the title with 46 points to edge Ontairio's 55 and Shelby's 78. Pleasant was fourth with 103 followed by Highland at 105, River Valley at 110 and Galion at 215. It is Harding's first league crown in boys XC in 21 years and its first in the MOAC. "There was a lot of stress coming into this meet because they wanted it so bad," Peters said. "Starting off the day, we were talking that this is just another race. It’s the next race so let’s go out here and do our best and whatever happens, happens. They really worked this whole season for this moment." For Harding, Andrew Tackett was third in 16 minutes, 48 seconds, Jackson Peters fourth in 16:58, Owen McCombs sixth in 17;15, Franklin Weaver 13th in 17:50, Deacon Durain 22nd in 18:34, Luke Estrada 29th in 19:00 and Trenton Estrada 30th in 19:01. "We were at the awards area where they were announcing the teams, and they got to second place. I was watching them and you could see the reaction when they announce Ontario second so they knew they won it. It was really good to see them get rewarded for their work they’ve done for this year," the coach said. For Harding's girls, Noel Stidham was the runner-up in 19:45 behind Shelby's Anna Will in 19:19 and just ahead of Pleasant's Madisyn Ruhe in third at 19:47 and Highland's Veronica Ballard in fourth at 19:53. "This is my 10 th year of coaching and that was one of the best races I’ve seen in all the years," Coach Peters said. "It was a great race to watch what she did there and come back like that and run as good as she did. It’s exciting to know she’s got two more years." More from the MOAC boys race Pleasant's Joey Dietsch was the boys individual champion with a 16:20, and River Valley's Kael Swartz was the runner-up in 16:35. Also for Pleasant were Turner Wilson (12th, 17:49), Jacob Meyers (19th, 18:14), Nathan Wagenblast (38th, 19:37) and Adam Stevens (42nd, 19:44). Behind Swartz for RV were Hager Adams (17th, 18:06), William Koon (23rd, 18:37), Harrison Lee (36th, 19:33), Iain Linville (41st, 19:42), Markus Parsons (44th, 19:55) and Brocktyn Caudill (51st, 20:13). For Highland, Jayden Marcum was 11th in 17:44 followed by Maddox Weiss (18th, 18:07), Ciaran Gilmore (25th, 18:40), Bodee Byler (26th, 18:48), Ben Sorrell (31st, 19:08), Carson Young (33rd, 19:15) and Sebastian Seaux (34th, 19:16).. item.title: NFL Expert Has Blunt Verdict on Patriots’ A.J. Brown Trade
item.description: NFL Expert Has Blunt Verdict on Patriots’ A.J. Brown Trade originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Patriots sent shockwaves throughout the NFL when they traded for A.J. Brown. The trade with the Eagles was meant to ensure the Patriots will return to the Super Bowl. However, since the trade, it hasn’t gone as planned for New England. Brown has played two games for the Patriots thanks to an ankle sprain he suffered in Week 1. He returned against the Jets on Sunday and earned 27 receiving yards. He dropped three attempts for the first time in his career. There appeared to be some rust after missing all that time. Many have wondered if the Patriots already regret trading for Brown. ESPN’s Dan Graziano reacted to that idea, calling it an overreaction. He stated that the team is 4-2 despite Brown's tough start, and "that tells you there's room for things to get a lot better." Coach Mike Vrabel said the team was " lucky to win ” following drops and multiple injuries. Brown later stated there are no excuses and that he’s going to put his best foot forward. The Patriots have a quick turnaround as they head to Chicago to face the Bears on Thursday. Graziano believes there’s nothing in Brown’s history indicating his struggles will continue. item.title: Ravens most to blame for another blown double-digit lead in Browns loss
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Ravens most to blame for another blown double-digit lead in Browns loss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It was a long day for the Baltimore Ravens , who missed too many opportunities. And Derrick Henry had another crucial fumble. And here are the Ravens most to blame for another blown double-digit lead in the loss to the Browns. Surprisingly, the Ravens took it on the chin against the Browns. They lost 13-10 in a game that caused a three-way tie for first place in the AFC North. The Ravens had a chance to flex, but they came up noodle-armed. So what went wrong? Let’s look at the blame list. Ravens RB Derrick Henry King Henry needs to close the deal. That’s all there is to it. In the fourth quarter, with his team leading and controlling the game throughout, Henry suffered the indignity of a punchout by Carson Schwesinger. Tyson Campbell fell on the ball at the Ravens’ 35-yard line. And the Ravens were unable to right the ship after the sudden change. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) It was Henry’s first fumble of the season. But the timing, like some of his fumbles in the past, was terrible. Henry owned his miscue , according to a post on X by Jamison Hensley. “I got to take care of the ball,” Henry said. “There’s no excuses for that. I got to be better. I put the team in harm’s way. (And) I sound like a broken record with this. But I got to go back to work on it. I told the team to put this one on me, and I just got to be better. Can’t put the team in that situation.” Henry is averaging just 4.1 yards per carry. That would be the worst average of his career. He’s averaging 4.9 for his career. And at the goal line ? Check out this post on X by Michael F. Florio. “I know he has a ton of TDs but … Derrick Henry has not been good at the goal line this season: 7 carries, -4 yds, 1 TD so far this season (counting today)” That leads to speculation that Henry may finally be slowing down after a Superman career, according to The Athletic. “At 32, you’re supposed to be about 54% of your career average, according to aging-curve data,” Michael Salfino wrote. “Counting Sunday, he’s averaging 4.1 yards per carry versus 5.6 the prior two years combined. The data seems to be fitting the age narrative, but maybe the cure is just getting Lamar Jackson back (possibly Week 7).” Yes, things should be better for Henry when Jackson gets back. And that’s why another Ravens player deserves to join the blame list. QB Tyler Huntley After playing great down the stretch in the overtime win over the Falcons, Huntley could not get things done throughout the game against the Browns. He completed only 19 of 31 passes for 165 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions. Also, Huntley carried five times for 28 yards. But Huntley couldn’t get the offense in rhythm. The team only needed a little rhythm to win this game. He missed open targets, and avoided disaster only when Browns safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren dropped an easy interception in the fourth quarter. Huntley gave the Browns’ defense plenty of credit , according to The Baltimore Banner. “Man, they were doing a good job of switching it up all throughout the game,” Huntley said. “I don’t know how many times I can say they changed it up, but they did a great job of switching it up every drive that we came out.” The offensive line didn’t help Huntley as much as expected. Left tackle Ronnie Stanley acknowledged it. “I think it just comes down to the details — lining up right, making sure you’re taking the right leverage on your block — and a lot of those plays come down to one block here or one person there,” Stanley said. “Putting us behind the sticks, it’s always going to be a long game if you keep doing that.” Yes, Huntley is a backup. But in today’s NFL, the backups have to get victories. The problem is the Ravens only needed an average performance from Huntley to win this game. They got below average, and the Browns stole one. Head coach Jesse Minter There’s no reason to give Minter a pass just because Jackson didn’t play. The Ravens’ defense couldn’t get it done with the game on the line, and that’s Minter’s baby. Maybe the Ravens just put the rookie coach in a situation where he would struggle to succeed, according to Sports Illustrated. “Allowing 130 yards and eight first downs and getting outscored, 10-0, in the final quarter in a 13-10 loss was all too familiar,” Jason La Canfora wrote. “Minter’s defense has already blown three double-digit leads and lost twice, and the disparity between his first half and second half defense is kind of sickening.” Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton said: “I’m not going to sound like a broken record. It’s ‘Groundhog Day’ with this question. I don’t know. I’m not going to give you an answer. I really don’t know.” The good news for the Ravens is that they stand in a three-way tie with the Browns and Steelers for first place in the AFC North. Related: Ravens’ Jesse Minter drops 1-word Lamar Jackson injury update after missing Browns game Related: Adam Schefter thinks Ravens’ Lamar Jackson returns for Bengals clash, but will he?

item.title: Chiefs Defensive Line Ends Historic Sack Drought
item.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs were about to join a very small, very unlucky club in NFL history. Entering Sunday’s game, the team was one of only three squads in the Super Bowl era to win three straight games without recording a single sack, according to reports. That ugly streak finally died in the second half. On Sunday, October 18, the defense finally located the quarterback amid the 22-6 victory against the Los Angeles Chargers. The drought ended with less than four minutes left in the third quarter when defensive end Ashton Gillotte tackled Justin Herbert. The Chiefs finished the day with four sacks total. Chris Jones and Peter Woods each got one. Chamarri Conner and George Karlaftis also added sacks late in the fourth quarter. It wasn’t just about the stats, though. The guys in the trenches were clearly frustrated by the lack of production. The Drive to Hit the Quarterback Ashton Gillotte, a second-year defensive end, didn’t hide his hunger for a big play. He told KSHB 41’s Tod Palmer, according to Yahoo Sports , “Obviously, that’s something we’ve been hunting up, and we’ve been longing for it.” He also noted that while “pressures are good, but that’s not what we pride ourselves on.” The pass rush has been inconsistent lately. Linebacker Drue Tranquill told the station that “teams have been getting the ball out quick on us.” It’s hard to live with that kind of efficiency. Still, the pressure is there. Karlaftis produced eight pressures across 38 pass rushes in the contest, according to reports. That was his second-highest single-game total in his career. The defensive front is finding its rhythm again. This season, Gillotte holds nine pressures alongside a 63.4 pass-rush grade as indicated by PFF data. For Woods, the win also marked his first career sack. Injury Concerns for the Offensive Line The win was a bit bittersweet because the cost was high. The Chiefs are already dealing with injuries to wide receivers Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton. Now, the right tackle position is in trouble. Jaylon Moore left the game after a heavy hit during the second quarter. Andy Reid confirmed the news after the game. “Jaylon Moore has a concussion,” Reid said. “That’s the one that stands out the most.” This is a massive blow to the unit. Earlier this season, starting left tackle Josh Simmons suffered a back injury, meaning the team already lost him. Moore is a $30 million player who signed his two-year deal in March 2025. Without him, the depth moves made during training camp, like bringing in Joshua Ezeudu, will be vital. The team hasn’t put Moore on injured reserve, so he stays on the active roster for now. Mahomes Maintains the Winning Streak While the defense worked on the sack drought, Patrick Mahomes kept the team at 5-0. He completed 23 of 30 passes for 272 yards. item.title: Bill Simmons doesn’t want to hear ‘the victim thing’ for Troy Aikman amid ESPN contract uncertainty
item.description: Credit: Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images / The Bill Simmons Podcast Bill Simmons has heard Troy Aikman’s account of his looming exit from ESPN, and he finds it about as convincing as Sean McVay calling a bubble screen on third down. On the latest episode of The Bill Simmons Podcast , Simmons poured cold water on the prevailing narrative that ESPN cast Aikman aside while rewarding Joe Buck, suggesting the network may simply have balked at Aikman’s asking price. Simmons, who left ESPN under acrimonious circumstances in 2015, said that experience taught him to distrust whichever version of a media breakup reaches the public first. “I feel like this is one of those classic sports media things where whatever the version of the story that somebody wanted to get out, got out first,” Simmons said. “But how do we know Aikman didn’t ask ESPN for like 25, 30 million? And they’re like, ‘Yeah, we’re not paying that.’ And now he’s taking umbrage. Meanwhile, he did this Miami thing already. I just, I don’t wanna hear the victim thing for Troy Aikman. He’s got a pretty good life.” Buck and Aikman, partners since 2002 at Fox and then ESPN, both entered 2026 in the final year of their contracts, and ESPN signed Buck to a six-year, $108 million extension last month without reaching a new deal with Aikman. Ryan Glasspiegel of Front Office Sports reported that the strain between the two boiled over into an argument before the Bills-Rams game at SoFi Stadium, and Aikman didn’t dispute it when he appeared on KTCK The Ticket in Dallas days later. That same night, Aikman told Jimmy Traina he expected ESPN to go in a different direction , noting that nobody had approached him about a new contract with the Super Bowl in February and his deal expiring in March. Simmons was hazier on the “Miami thing” than on the money, at one point wondering aloud whether Aikman had acquired some kind of ownership stake in the Dolphins. He hadn’t, though his involvement in Miami grew far beyond what anyone envisioned when it began. Adam Schefter reported in January that the Dolphins hired Aikman as a consultant for their general manager search after firing Chris Grier, roughly a month after Aikman said he was “flabbergasted” by Mike McDaniel’s bizarre fourth-quarter management in a Monday Night Football loss to the Steelers. ESPN insisted the arrangement didn’t interfere with his broadcasting duties , and the role was billed as temporary, but Aikman stayed on to help with the head coaching search after McDaniel was fired New head coach Jeff Hafley later described Aikman as a trusted sounding board , and Aikman raised eyebrows across the league by explaining on the Cowboys’ DLLS podcast that Miami valued his relationships and the information he could obtain that the team couldn’t. item.content:encoded: Credit: Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images / The Bill Simmons Podcast Bill Simmons has heard Troy Aikman’s account of his looming exit from ESPN, and he finds it about as convincing as Sean McVay calling a bubble screen on third down. On the latest episode of The Bill Simmons Podcast , Simmons poured cold water on the prevailing narrative that ESPN cast Aikman aside while rewarding Joe Buck, suggesting the network may simply have balked at Aikman’s asking price. Simmons, who left ESPN under acrimonious circumstances in 2015, said that experience taught him to distrust whichever version of a media breakup reaches the public first. “I feel like this is one of those classic sports media things where whatever the version of the story that somebody wanted to get out, got out first,” Simmons said. “But how do we know Aikman didn’t ask ESPN for like 25, 30 million? And they’re like, ‘Yeah, we’re not paying that.’ And now he’s taking umbrage. Meanwhile, he did this Miami thing already. I just, I don’t wanna hear the victim thing for Troy Aikman. He’s got a pretty good life.” Buck and Aikman, partners since 2002 at Fox and then ESPN, both entered 2026 in the final year of their contracts, and ESPN signed Buck to a six-year, $108 million extension last month without reaching a new deal with Aikman. Ryan Glasspiegel of Front Office Sports reported that the strain between the two boiled over into an argument before the Bills-Rams game at SoFi Stadium, and Aikman didn’t dispute it when he appeared on KTCK The Ticket in Dallas days later. That same night, Aikman told Jimmy Traina he expected ESPN to go in a different direction , noting that nobody had approached him about a new contract with the Super Bowl in February and his deal expiring in March. Simmons was hazier on the “Miami thing” than on the money, at one point wondering aloud whether Aikman had acquired some kind of ownership stake in the Dolphins. He hadn’t, though his involvement in Miami grew far beyond what anyone envisioned when it began. Adam Schefter reported in January that the Dolphins hired Aikman as a consultant for their general manager search after firing Chris Grier, roughly a month after Aikman said he was “flabbergasted” by Mike McDaniel’s bizarre fourth-quarter management in a Monday Night Football loss to the Steelers. ESPN insisted the arrangement didn’t interfere with his broadcasting duties , and the role was billed as temporary, but Aikman stayed on to help with the head coaching search after McDaniel was fired New head coach Jeff Hafley later described Aikman as a trusted sounding board , and Aikman raised eyebrows across the league by explaining on the Cowboys’ DLLS podcast that Miami valued his relationships and the information he could obtain that the team couldn’t. That arrangement has since wound down, with Mark Maske of Front Office Sports reporting last week that Aikman no longer has a formal, ongoing consulting agreement with Miami, but not before it invited a year’s worth of conflict-of-interest questions about the man calling the league’s Monday night showcase. Aikman’s now-former side gig is a large part of why Simmons can’t summon much sympathy. He pointed out that Aikman calls 17 regular-season games a year, flies around the country to do it, and would see ESPN draw virtually the same audience for those games whether he’s in the booth or not. When Cousin Sal noted that Simmons usually champions talent banding together in negotiations, Simmons granted that Buck and Aikman hadn’t done that, but questioned the assumption that Buck was the one who broke ranks. In his telling, the pair could have pulled a “Friends” cast maneuver and negotiated as a unit, unless Aikman believed he was worth more than Buck. “I don’t believe any of this stuff because I’ve been through it where people have written things about stuff I’ve been involved with or whatever, and it’s always like whatever the first narrative that comes out becomes the narrative,” Simmons said. “And in this case, I don’t believe it.” Simmons also handed ESPN a blueprint for life after Aikman, proposing that the network jettison the ManningCast altogether and give Peyton and Eli Manning eight games apiece in the main booth. The Athletic’s Andrew Marchand floated a similar arrangement last month, identifying the Mannings as a plausible successor to Aikman, though Puck’s John Ourand recently reported that his most reliable sources expect Greg Olsen to inherit the seat once his Fox contract expires and he’s free to chase the No. 1 job he lost to Tom Brady. Whatever number Aikman put in front of ESPN, Simmons isn’t worried about where he’ll end up, and a quick survey of the league’s other top booths suggests he has good reason to be confident. CBS put Tony Romo on leave after his July arrest in Milwaukee and severed ties with him earlier this month, leaving J.J. Watt to call the rest of the season alongside Jim Nantz with no long-term successor in place, while Amazon recently extended Kirk Herbstreit on Thursday Night Football in a deal that reportedly lets the streamer move on if one of its top targets becomes available, with McVay being chief among them. Simmons would happily speed up that process, though. “Speaking of TV, Sean McVay, just go to Amazon already,” Simmons said. “Just do it now, do it in time for Week 7. They have the Herbstreit job waiting for you. Just go next week.” “Just two weeks in a row of atrocious coaching from [Sean McVay].” @BillSimmons and @TheCousinSal on Sean McVay’s coaching troubles and the Rams’ shocking loss to the Cardinals. https://t.co/GCFMXbpN5S — The Ringer (@ringer) October 19, 2026 ESPN might have one waiting, too, if Aikman is right about the network moving on when his contract expires in March. The post Bill Simmons doesn’t want to hear ‘the victim thing’ for Troy Aikman amid ESPN contract uncertainty appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Mariners’ New Manager Candidate Brings One Question Seattle Must Answer
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - MAY 07: A Seattle Mariners hat is seen before the game against the Tampa Bay Rays at T-Mobile Park on May 07, 2022 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty ATLANTA, GEORGIA - APRIL 20: Manager Rocco Baldelli #5 of the Minnesota Twins looks on during the fifth inning against the Atlanta Braves at Truist Park on April 20, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 27: Manager Dan Wilson #6 of the Seattle Mariners looks on prior to the game against the Los Angeles Angels at T-Mobile Park on September 27, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) Getty The Seattle Mariners have another experienced name to consider as they search for a replacement for Dan Wilson. Rocco Baldelli has emerged as a candidate, according to Adam Jude of The Seattle Times, who reported that Seattle is expected to speak with the former Minnesota Twins manager. The connection makes sense. Baldelli managed Minnesota for seven seasons and spent 2026 as a special assistant in the Los Angeles Dodgers’ front office. However, his résumé should only be the start of Seattle’s evaluation. The Mariners need to determine how Baldelli would address this roster’s problems, particularly when deciding who plays, how hitters prepare, and when established plans need to change. That requires specific answers about Seattle’s players before the organization makes another consequential hire. Rocco Baldelli Gives Mariners an Experienced Option Getty Manager Rocco Baldelli #5 of the Minnesota Twins looks on during the fifth inning against the Atlanta Braves at Truist Park on April 20, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Baldelli finished his Twins tenure with a 527-505 record and three American League Central titles. He earned AL Manager of the Year honors after Minnesota won 101 games in 2019. His first Twins team also set an MLB record with 307 home runs . Those accomplishments show he can run a successful Major League clubhouse. They do not establish that the same approach would automatically work in Seattle. The Mariners should ask how he would construct consistent roles around Julio Rodríguez, Cal Raleigh and Josh Naylor while bringing younger hitters into the lineup. They should also ask when he would prioritize a platoon advantage and when a player needs an extended opportunity against different pitching. No universal answer exists to either question. A useful interview would require Baldelli to explain his choices using Seattle’s actual roster. That would reveal more than a discussion focused entirely on his previous division championships or the organization he most recently worked for. Seattle should also ask him to describe a decision that failed in Minnesota, the information he used at the time, and what he would change now. That would make the evaluation more concrete. Rocco Baldelli Gives Mariners an Experienced Option Getty Manager Rocco Baldelli #5 of the Minnesota Twins looks on during the fifth inning against the Atlanta Braves at Truist Park on April 20, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Baldelli finished his Twins tenure with a 527-505 record and three American League Central titles. He earned AL Manager of the Year honors after Minnesota won 101 games in 2019. His first Twins team also set an MLB record with 307 home runs . Those accomplishments show he can run a successful Major League clubhouse. They do not establish that the same approach would automatically work in Seattle. The Mariners should ask how he would construct consistent roles around Julio Rodríguez, Cal Raleigh and Josh Naylor while bringing younger hitters into the lineup. They should also ask when he would prioritize a platoon advantage and when a player needs an extended opportunity against different pitching. No universal answer exists to either question. A useful interview would require Baldelli to explain his choices using Seattle’s actual roster. That would reveal more than a discussion focused entirely on his previous division championships or the organization he most recently worked for. Seattle should also ask him to describe a decision that failed in Minnesota, the information he used at the time, and what he would change now. That would make the evaluation more concrete. Read More From Heavy Mariners Reportedly Eyeing World Series Winner As Next Manager Seattle’s Next Manager Needs More Than a Résumé Getty Manager Dan Wilson #6 of the Seattle Mariners looks on prior to the game against the Los Angeles Angels at T-Mobile Park on September 27, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) Seattle has already moved on from Wilson and several coaches . The next step should establish which responsibilities belong to the manager and which changes the front office must make. A manager can clarify preparation, communicate playing time, and respond when performance slips. He cannot personally acquire another impact hitter or manufacture healthy pitching depth. Seattle should seek a candidate who can explain what he would change immediately, what requires additional personnel, and how he would raise concerns with baseball operations. The organization should then give those recommendations enough authority to matter. Jude’s report signals interest, not a completed interview or an agreement. Baldelli remains one option in an ongoing search. If Seattle advances those conversations, the most useful question is straightforward: What would he do differently with these Mariners? His answer should carry more weight than his name’s familiarity. item.title: Westlake Chaps hold onto No. 1 spot in this week's Central Texas volleyball power poll

item.title: Sophie Cunningham’s ‘MAGA Barbie’ label draws attention after Donald Trump’s controversial compliment
item.description: Source: jctabb/Depositphotos Sophie Cunningham’s name has become part of a political conversation that stretches well beyond the WNBA, and Donald Trump’s latest remarks have brought that attention back into focus. The Indiana Fever guard was singled out by the president during an October 12 rally in Youngstown, Ohio, where he praised her appearance while questioning her basketball ability. The remarks renewed attention on Cunningham’s “MAGA Barbie” nickname, a label that has followed her as audiences have debated her political image and interpreted her social media presence and public comments. Cunningham, however, has pushed back against attempts to place her neatly in one political camp. That contrast between her own description of her beliefs and the public image built around her has become another part of her increasingly high-profile WNBA career. Donald Trump’s comments put Cunningham back in the spotlight Trump referred to Cunningham as a “beautiful young woman” during his October 12 appearance in Youngstown. He suggested that her presence could help attract spectators before joking that she would not necessarily help a team score points. The comments immediately shifted attention from Cunningham’s basketball career to her broader public image. Rather than discussing her shooting, defense or role with Indiana, Trump focused largely on her appearance and ability to attract an audience. That attention arrived shortly after Cunningham completed another season with the Fever. Indiana’s 2026 campaign ended with a first-round playoff loss to the Las Vegas Aces, sending Cunningham into an offseason in which her future with the team remains uncertain. Why the ‘MAGA Barbie’ label follows Cunningham The “MAGA Barbie” nickname was circulating before Trump mentioned Cunningham in October. It reflects the way some fans, commentators, and political audiences have interpreted her public image and perceived political leanings. The label has also been fueled by the increasingly political attention surrounding Cunningham outside basketball. Her social media activity and willingness to express her opinions publicly have led people to assume where she stands politically. Cunningham has rejected the idea that those assumptions tell the whole story. She has described herself as “very much in the middle,” saying she agrees with some positions on both sides of the political spectrum and disagrees with others. That makes the nickname more of a reflection of public perception than a formal description of Cunningham’s own political identity. Cunningham has resisted being placed in one political camp Cunningham has acknowledged that people frequently make assumptions about her beliefs. In discussing her politics, she has emphasized that her views do not fit neatly into a single partisan category.
