As their relationship develops, they must confront personal fears and a secret that threatens to come between them. Directed by Biodun Stephen, the romantic drama explores love, trust and the difficult choices that can test a relationship. The film also gives viewers another opportunity to see the chemistry between the two actors as romantic leads. Unexpected Places Bimbo Ademoye plays Prosper, the daughter of a housekeeper who steps in to manage the household while her mother recovers from surgery. Her new responsibilities bring her into contact with Chris, played by Timini Egbuson, a wealthy playboy whose irresponsible behaviour has become a concern for his father. Their relationship begins on difficult terms, but Prosper’s presence gradually challenges Chris to reconsider his choices and take responsibility for his life. Produced by Ademoye and directed by Great Val Edochie, the romantic drama explores personal growth, love and the unexpected circumstances that can change people’s lives. The film also takes a more emotional turn as the couple’s relationship develops. Introducing the Kujus Directed by Biodun Stephen, Introducing the Kujus is a family comedy-drama set in Badagry, Lagos. The film follows five siblings who are reluctant to return to their hometown for the fifth anniversary of their mother’s death. Mausi Kuju, played by Bisola Aiyeola, and her brother Maugbe, played by Timini Egbuson, devise a plan to bring the family together, but their complicated relationships threaten to get in the way. Bimbo Ademoye plays Ebi, one of the siblings whose relationships and family history contribute to the story. The film explores family bonds, old disagreements and the things that can bring people back together. item.title: Christian Pulisic is no longer a focal point for the US or Milan – and that’s OK
item.description: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied Usually, the second weekend of October sees Christian Pulisic flanked by compatriots as the Star-Spangled Banner plays. Last year, he was involved in US friendlies against Ecuador and Australia. But this year, with Fifa having folded the October window into September, Pulisic didn’t have the chance. On Sunday, his pre-match music was O Generosa, the Serie A anthem, which he observed with a soft smile. Mark Twain’s first visit to Italy left him describing the country as “a vast museum of magnificence and misery”, and it’s a fitting summary of Pulisic’s three-plus years with Milan. The magnificence: 43 goals and 25 assists in 138 appearances. The misery: just one trophy since he arrived in July 2023, a 2025 Supercoppa Italia held in Saudi Arabia. Continue reading...

item.title: Midea Launches WIN 9JA WIN Promotion with Guaranteed Rewards and Chery Tiggo 2 Pro Grand Prize
item.description: Midea has announced the launch of WIN 9JA WIN , a nationwide consumer promotion designed to reward Nigerians who choose Midea home appliances during the 2026 festive shopping season. Running from 10 October to 31 December 2026 , the promotion gives every qualifying shopper an instant opportunity to win, with a Chery Tiggo 2 Pro positioned as the ultimate grand prize. Under the promotion, consumers who purchase any Midea product worth ₦100,000 or more from a participating dealer receive a scratch voucher at the point of purchase. The shopper scratches the voucher to reveal the reward won, creating a simple and immediate link between purchase and reward. Every qualifying shopper is a winner, subject to the approved campaign terms and conditions. The campaign combines retail participation with radio, digital, public relations, in-store visibility and an extensive on-ground Promo Tour Truck programme. The touring activation will carry the excitement of WIN 9JA WIN into selected markets and dealer locations, with the Chery Tiggo 2 Pro prominently showcased to give consumers a close view of the campaign’s headline prize. A Consumer Promotion Built Around Instant Reward WIN 9JA WIN is designed to make the festive purchase journey more rewarding while strengthening engagement between Midea , its dealer network and consumers across Nigeria. Its central proposition is straightforward: make a qualifying purchase, receive a scratch voucher and discover the reward immediately. The approved reward pool spans Midea home appliances and branded consumer gifts. These include side-by-side refrigerators, chest freezers, air conditioners, refrigerators, washing machines, air fryers, microwave ovens, kettles, standing fans and blenders, as well as branded T-shirts, caps and pens. The ultimate reward is a Chery Tiggo 2 Pro, presented in the campaign materials as the car to be won. MIDEA NIGERIA | MEDIA RELEASE How Consumers Can Participate Step Consumer action Purchase Buy any Midea product or combination of eligible Midea products worth ₦100,000 or more from a participating dealer between 10 October and 31 December 2026. Receive Collect the campaign scratch voucher issued for the qualifying purchase. Scratch Scratch the voucher to reveal the reward. Claim Follow the verification and prize-claim guidance provided by the participating dealer in accordance with the approved campaign terms and conditions. Additional Midea Air Conditioner Offer Alongside WIN 9JA WIN, Midea is also offering free installation and a free copper kit to consumers who purchase any Midea air conditioner from 1 October through 31 December 2026. The offer extends the campaign’s value beyond the product purchase by helping eligible AC buyers with installation support, subject to the applicable terms and conditions. Promo Tour Truck Takes WIN 9JA WIN Closer to Consumers A major feature of the campaign is the branded Promo Tour Truck programme, developed as a mobile visibility and engagement platform.

A Consumer Promotion Built Around Instant Reward WIN 9JA WIN is designed to make the festive purchase journey more rewarding while strengthening engagement between Midea , its dealer network and consumers across Nigeria. Its central proposition is straightforward: make a qualifying purchase, receive a scratch voucher and discover the reward immediately. The approved reward pool spans Midea home appliances and branded consumer gifts. These include side-by-side refrigerators, chest freezers, air conditioners, refrigerators, washing machines, air fryers, microwave ovens, kettles, standing fans and blenders, as well as branded T-shirts, caps and pens. The ultimate reward is a Chery Tiggo 2 Pro, presented in the campaign materials as the car to be won. MIDEA NIGERIA | MEDIA RELEASE How Consumers Can Participate Step Consumer action Purchase Buy any Midea product or combination of eligible Midea products worth ₦100,000 or more from a participating dealer between 10 October and 31 December 2026. Receive Collect the campaign scratch voucher issued for the qualifying purchase. Scratch Scratch the voucher to reveal the reward. Claim Follow the verification and prize-claim guidance provided by the participating dealer in accordance with the approved campaign terms and conditions. Additional Midea Air Conditioner Offer Alongside WIN 9JA WIN, Midea is also offering free installation and a free copper kit to consumers who purchase any Midea air conditioner from 1 October through 31 December 2026. The offer extends the campaign’s value beyond the product purchase by helping eligible AC buyers with installation support, subject to the applicable terms and conditions. Promo Tour Truck Takes WIN 9JA WIN Closer to Consumers A major feature of the campaign is the branded Promo Tour Truck programme, developed as a mobile visibility and engagement platform. The vehicle format is designed to operate as a moving billboard and activation hub, carrying Midea branding, product communication and WIN 9JA WIN messaging through high-traffic retail corridors and participating dealer locations. The Chery Tiggo 2 Pro will be prominently showcased as part of the tour, allowing shoppers and local communities to see the campaign’s ultimate prize at close range. At scheduled dealer stops, consumers will be able to discover Midea products, receive clear information about the promotion and understand the qualifying purchase and scratch-voucher process. The programme is intended to support participating dealers, stimulate retail interest and bring the promotion into the communities where consumers shop. Selected Tour Markets and Dealer Locations The supplied tour schedule covers selected locations across Lagos, the South-West, South-South, South- East, North-Central and Northern Nigeria. The dealer activation routes are scheduled from 10 October to 1 November 2026, subject to final operational confirmation. The market clusters are listed below; the detailed dealer-location appendix forms part of this release pack. East Route : Port Harcourt, Aba, Umuahia, Uyo and Oron, Owerri, Nnewi, Onitsha, Awka, Asaba and Enugu. Lagos and adjoining markets : Lekki, Victoria Island, Ikoyi, Ajah, Lagos Island, Idumota, Apapa, Festac, Alaba, Ojo, Ikotun, Igando, Idimu, Ipaja, Abule Egba, Agege, Ikeja, Allen, Maryland, Ogba, Yaba, Surulere, Ebute Metta, Ikorodu, Badagry, Ota, Agbara and Isheri. South-West and South-South route: Ibadan, Iseyin, Ogbomoso, Ilorin, Osogbo, Ilesa, Ile-Ife, Abeokuta, Sagamu, Ijebu-Ode, Ago-Iwoye, Mowe, Warri, Effurun, Ughelli, Sapele, Benin City, Irrua, Uromi, Akure and Ondo. North and North-Central Route: Abuja, Mararaba, Lokoja, Makurdi, Lafia, Kaduna, Kano, Yola and Jimeta. Supporting Retail Engagement and Household Choice The campaign reflects Midea’s focus on making home-appliance technology more accessible and relevant to Nigerian households. By combining guaranteed rewards with a wide dealer footprint and direct market engagement, WIN 9JA WIN gives consumers another reason to explore Midea’s range of air conditioners, refrigerators, freezers, washing machines, cooking appliances and small domestic appliances during the year-end season. Executive Comment / Quotation “WIN 9JA WIN is our way of thanking Nigerian consumers and making every qualifying purchase more rewarding. The mechanic is simple, transparent and immediate: buy, receive a scratch voucher and reveal your reward. Through the Promo Tour Truck programme, we are also taking the campaign closer to our dealer partners and consumers in markets across the country, while giving shoppers the opportunity to experience Midea products and see the Chery Tiggo 2 Pro grand prize up close.” – Ashok Dimri, Business Head, Africa, of Care Global Consumer Ltd. Call to Action Consumers can visit participating Midea dealers nationwide between 10 October and 31 December 2026, purchase eligible Midea products worth ₦100,000 or more and collect a scratch voucher to reveal their reward. Consumers purchasing any Midea air conditioner can also access the free installation and free copper kit offer through 31 December 2026, subject to the applicable terms and conditions. About Midea Group Midea is one of over 10 brands operating under the Smart Home Business of Midea Group. Midea Group , with the vision of “bringing great innovations to life”, is an international tech-leading company which specializes in seven major business areas: Smart Home, Industrial Technologies, Building Technologies, KUKA, New Energy, Midea Healthcare and ANNTO Logistics. Midea’s products and services have served more than 500 million customers worldwide, including key clients and strategic partners across various industries. Midea operates more than 400 subsidiaries, 41 R&D centres and 65 major manufacturing bases globally, with a business network covering over 200 countries and regions. item.title: Apple AirPods 5 review: the best open-fit earbuds yet
item.description: Upgraded, cheaper AirPods have noise cancelling, sound and controls to rival many plugged-in buds but without tips Apple’s latest AirPods set a new standard for open-fit buds with upgraded noise cancelling that now rivals many plugged-in designs of the same price. The AirPods 5 have the same design the popular AirPods 4 offering an option for those that do not like silicone ear tips used by most noise cancelling earbuds. They come in two versions, with or without a wireless charging case and swipe controls, costing from £119 (€149/$129/A$219) – £10 cheaper than the launch price of their predecessors . Connectivity: Bluetooth 5.3, SBC, AAC, H2 chip Battery life: four or five hours with ANC (22 hours with case) Water resistance: IP57 (up to 1 metre for 30 minutes ) Earbud dimensions: 30.2 x 18.3 x 18.1mm Earbud weight: 4.3g each Charging case dimensions: 46.2 x 50.1 x 21.2mm Charging case weight: 32.3g/34.7g Case charging: USB-C or wireless (Qi or Watch) Continue reading...

item.title: Winning is not enough for Manchester City to move on from this crisis | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. But consider his assessment of Manchester City’s 3-0 win at Liverpool on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.title: Welcome home, Sophie Adenot
item.description: Video: 00:02:54 After 237 days and over 3,700 orbits around Earth aboard the International Space Station, Sophie Adenot is back on Earth! Following a handover to Crew-13, Sophie and her Crew-12 crewmates undocked on 7 October and splashed down off the coast of California the next day. Now back in Europe, Sophie will begin her post-flight data collection and rehabilitation while readjusting to life on Earth after the longest mission in space by a European astronaut so far. Welcome home, Sophie!

item.title: TCL West Africa Regional Launch in Côte d’Ivoire: Showcases 2026 SQD Mini LED TVs and Smart Home Innovations
item.description: TCL , a global leader in consumer electronics and No.1 Mini LED and Ultra Large Screen TV Brand (75”+)¹, has showcased its latest consumer electronics and home appliance portfolio for Nigeria during its West Africa regional launch event in Côte d’Ivoire. Bringing together media, business partners, retailers, distributors, industry stakeholders and content creators from across the region, the event provided a closer look at TCL’s 2026 display innovations alongside new solutions across air conditioning, refrigeration, laundry and monitors. The launch reflects TCL’s continued investment in Nigeria and its focus on introducing technologies that respond to the way consumers across both markets live today. From larger screens for sport and family entertainment to energy conscious cooling, high capacity appliances and connected home experiences, the new portfolio has been developed to combine performance, convenience and accessibility. Daniel Ray , Director of Sales, TCL West Africa, said: “ Nigeria are important markets within TCL’s West Africa growth strategy, with consumers increasingly looking for technology that delivers strong performance while remaining relevant to their everyday needs. Through this regional launch, we are bringing together entertainment, cooling and home appliance innovations designed around how people live, connect and enjoy content across both markets. Our ambition is to continue making advanced technology more accessible while giving consumers greater choice across the home. “ A New Era of Premium Big Screen Entertainment Large screen entertainment continues to grow across Nigeria, with consumers increasingly seeking more immersive experiences across sport, movies, streaming and gaming. Leading TCL’s latest television portfolio is the C7L SQD Mini LED range, available from 65 to 98 inches, bringing enhanced colour precision, brightness control, deeper blacks and improved halo control. Complementing the C7L is the 98 inch C6K QD Mini LED TV, delivering an ultra large screen experience with advanced Mini LED performance for movies, live sport and gaming. TCL Brings Premium Large Screen Entertainment to Nigeria with the C7L SQD Mini LED TV The TCL C7L brings the latest generation of SQD Mini LED technology to consumers across Nigeria, with screen sizes ranging from 65 to 98 inches. Designed for immersive home entertainment, it combines advanced Mini LED light control, enhanced colour precision and strong contrast performance across sport, movies, streaming and gaming. Complementing the C7L is the 98 inch C6K QD Mini LED TV, delivering an ultra large screen experience with advanced Mini LED performance for movies, live sport and gaming. TCL Brings Premium Large Screen Entertainment to Nigeria with the C7L SQD Mini LED TV The TCL C7L brings the latest generation of SQD Mini LED technology to consumers across Nigeria, with screen sizes ranging from 65 to 98 inches. Designed for immersive home entertainment, it combines advanced Mini LED light control, enhanced colour precision and strong contrast performance across sport, movies, streaming and gaming. The 98 inch model features up to 2,176 Precise Dimming Zones, up to HDR 3,000 nits brightness, up to 100% BT.2020 All Scenes Wide Color Gamut, an HVA 2.0 Pro Panel, Audio by Bang & Olufsen and a 288Hz VRR Game Accelerator. TCL C6K QD Mini LED TV Expands the Ultra Large Screen Experience TCL C6K QD Mini LED TV complements an immersive ultra large screen experience with screen sizes ranging from 65 to 98 inches, combining QD-Mini LED backlighting with quantum dot colour technology for enhanced brightness, contrast and colour performance. It features TCL All Domain Halo Control Technology, up to 512 Precise Dimming Zones, a 144Hz native refresh rate, an AiPQ Pro Processor, a Matte HVA Panel and an ONKYO 2.1 Hi Fi audio system. Smarter Cooling Designed for Local Climate Needs With warm temperatures forming part of everyday life across Nigeria, cooling performance, energy management and convenience remain important considerations for households. TCL highlighted two air conditioning solutions designed to address these priorities, the FreshIN 3.0 and SaveIN AI Series 24K. TCL FreshIN 3.0 FreshIN 3.0 expands the air conditioning experience beyond temperature control by introducing fresh outdoor air into the room while supporting improved indoor air quality. Key technologies include FreshIN Technology, T AI Energy Saving, Smart Voice Control, QuadruPuri filtration, Visible Air Quality and Gentle Breeze. The system is also engineered for stable operation in high ambient temperatures, making it especially relevant for consumers across Nigeria seeking reliable cooling performance during hotter periods of the year. TCL SaveIN AI Series The TCL SaveIN AI Series is designed around efficient everyday cooling, combining T AI Energy Saving, smart Wi Fi control and Coanda Airflow. Its intelligent energy management technology dynamically adjusts compressor performance based on temperature conditions, helping consumers manage cooling more efficiently while maintaining indoor comfort. For households conscious of both comfort and electricity consumption, the SaveIN AI Series offers a smarter approach to everyday cooling through intelligent controls and flexible energy management. Refrigeration Designed for Local Households For many households across Nigeria, refrigeration needs extend beyond everyday food storage to larger family shopping, meal preparation and the need to keep food fresh for longer. TCL’s latest refrigeration range addresses these priorities through generous capacity, flexible storage and reliable cooling, led by the P7 Side by Side Refrigerator and C7 Cross Door Refrigerator. TCL P7 Side by Side Refrigerator The TCL P774SBBG is a large capacity side by side refrigerator designed for households that require generous storage space for fresh and frozen food. Featuring a premium black glass finish, the model combines No Frost cooling, inverter technology, electronic controls and multi airflow functionality to support consistent cooling and convenient food organisation. Its larger format makes it particularly suited to family households looking for greater storage flexibility without compromising on contemporary kitchen design. TCL C7 Cross Door Refrigerator The TCL C780CDN introduces a spacious four door format that allows households to organise groceries, frozen food and everyday essentials more easily. Combining No Frost cooling with inverter performance, the model has been designed around flexibility, capacity and convenience, responding to the needs of households looking for practical food storage alongside a premium kitchen aesthetic. Smarter Laundry for Busy Households with the TCL C5 Washer Dryer The TCL C5 washer dryer combines a 12 kg washing capacity with TCL Super Drum technology, providing additional washing space and improved fabric movement. Its feature set includes Auto Dose, jetBubble technology, Wi Fi connectivity, Steam Wash, activeFresh, Dynamic Rinse and quick wash programmes. The large capacity format is particularly suited to family households, while its connected features and automatic washing functions help reduce the effort required for everyday laundry and fabric care. Strengthening TCL’s Presence Across Nigeria The regional launch underlines TCL’s strategy to strengthen its presence across Nigeria through a broader product ecosystem and closer collaboration with local distributors, retailers, media and technology communities. By combining global product innovation with a stronger understanding of local consumer priorities, TCL aims to deliver products that are relevant across different areas of everyday life, from entertainment and cooling to food storage, laundry and connected displays. Daniel Ray added: “Our focus is to strengthen TCL’s presence market by market, with products that respond to the needs of the consumers we serve. In Nigeria, that means bringing together larger and more immersive entertainment, efficient cooling, greater household capacity and smarter connected experiences. We see significant potential across both markets and will continue working closely with our partners to make TCL technology more widely available.” Availability Product sizes, specifications, pricing and availability may vary by market. For further information, please visit SIMS Nigeria https://simsng.com/tcl-store/ . About TCL TCL is a leading consumer electronics brand and leader in the global television industry.

item.title: “A Girl Who Learns Is a Girl Who Is Not a Bride” – Obiageli “Oby” Ezekwesili
item.description: A girl who learns is not a bride. Today, the world is asked to end child marriage and invest in girls’ rights. I join that call wearing three hats: as a member of the advisory council behind Columbia University’s report Accelerating Efforts to End Child Marriage ; as Civil Society Representative on the Steering Committee of the African Union’s Decade of Accelerated Action for the Transformation of Education and Skills Development in Africa (2025–2034); and as the leader of Human Capital Africa, an organisation that has spent years arguing that Africa’s human capital crisis begins in the early-grade classroom. UNICEF’s 2026 estimates show that about one in five girls worldwide is married before 18. That adds up to roughly 650 million women and girls alive today who were married as children. More than 12 million girls are still married each year, about one every three seconds, and sub-Saharan Africa has the highest prevalence at 31 per cent. In Nigeria, 23.6 million women and girls were married before 18, the largest number in West and Central Africa. In parts of the North, the situation is a national emergency: in Jigawa, 78 per cent of women aged 20–49 were first married before 18, and 63 per cent of women left school to marry. The cost of inaction is high . Our Columbia report includes new analysis by the Centre for Global Development. It estimates losses of up to $175 billion a year, or almost $2.5 trillion by 2040, from lost productivity and higher health risks caused by child marriage. The report also warns that aid cuts, weakening global commitment to women’s rights, and rising conflict could slow or reverse progress. Child marriage is not a side issue in development. It drains a nation’s human capital directly. Progress is possible . An estimated 68 million child marriages have been averted over the past 25 years, through girls’ education, legal reform and social protection. The evidence on what works is strong: Each year of secondary education lowers a girl’s chance of marrying before 18 by five percentage points or more. In Niger, when the government removed the direct costs of middle school for rural girls, each additional year in secondary school was associated with a 19 percentage point lower probability of marriage. If every African girl completed secondary education, child marriage could be almost eliminated. Where HCA’s mission and this campaign meet, a girl cannot stay in secondary school if she never learned to read. Today, 89 per cent of children in sub-Saharan Africa are in learning poverty, unable to read and understand a simple text by age ten. A girl who cannot read by ten falls behind, then drops out. Once she is out of school, she is at the greatest risk of marriage. That is why we say schooling is not learning. Foundational literacy and numeracy are the first and cheapest protection a girl has. item.dc:creator: BellaNaija Features
item.content:encoded: A girl who learns is not a bride. Today, the world is asked to end child marriage and invest in girls’ rights. I join that call wearing three hats: as a member of the advisory council behind Columbia University’s report Accelerating Efforts to End Child Marriage ; as Civil Society Representative on the Steering Committee of the African Union’s Decade of Accelerated Action for the Transformation of Education and Skills Development in Africa (2025–2034); and as the leader of Human Capital Africa, an organisation that has spent years arguing that Africa’s human capital crisis begins in the early-grade classroom. UNICEF’s 2026 estimates show that about one in five girls worldwide is married before 18. That adds up to roughly 650 million women and girls alive today who were married as children. More than 12 million girls are still married each year, about one every three seconds, and sub-Saharan Africa has the highest prevalence at 31 per cent. In Nigeria, 23.6 million women and girls were married before 18, the largest number in West and Central Africa. In parts of the North, the situation is a national emergency: in Jigawa, 78 per cent of women aged 20–49 were first married before 18, and 63 per cent of women left school to marry. The cost of inaction is high . Our Columbia report includes new analysis by the Centre for Global Development. It estimates losses of up to $175 billion a year, or almost $2.5 trillion by 2040, from lost productivity and higher health risks caused by child marriage. The report also warns that aid cuts, weakening global commitment to women’s rights, and rising conflict could slow or reverse progress. Child marriage is not a side issue in development. It drains a nation’s human capital directly. Progress is possible . An estimated 68 million child marriages have been averted over the past 25 years, through girls’ education, legal reform and social protection. The evidence on what works is strong: Each year of secondary education lowers a girl’s chance of marrying before 18 by five percentage points or more. In Niger, when the government removed the direct costs of middle school for rural girls, each additional year in secondary school was associated with a 19 percentage point lower probability of marriage. If every African girl completed secondary education, child marriage could be almost eliminated. Where HCA’s mission and this campaign meet, a girl cannot stay in secondary school if she never learned to read. Today, 89 per cent of children in sub-Saharan Africa are in learning poverty, unable to read and understand a simple text by age ten. A girl who cannot read by ten falls behind, then drops out. Once she is out of school, she is at the greatest risk of marriage. That is why we say schooling is not learning. Foundational literacy and numeracy are the first and cheapest protection a girl has. At the Columbia launch, I said that community programmes and advocacy are not enough on their own. Governments must lead. On this Day of the Girl, Human Capital Africa calls on African governments to: Make foundational learning a girl-protection policy. Every girl should be reading with comprehension by age ten, using proven methods such as structured pedagogy and Teaching at the Right Level. Guarantee the move into secondary school. Remove fees, uniform and transport costs for girls, especially in rural communities with high rates of child marriage. Enforce 18 as the minimum age of marriage in law and in practice, in every state and every community, with traditional and religious leaders as partners. Fund this domestically. As foreign aid shrinks, African budgets and African philanthropy must take over. Measure and publish. Track girls’ learning, their transition to secondary school, and child marriage rates in national accountability systems. The AU Decade of Education gives Africa ten years and a continental mandate. As a member of its Steering Committee, I will press for girls’ learning and retention to be at the centre of how the Decade’s success is measured. A Decade that does not end child marriage will not have transformed African education. The Columbia report sets a realistic target: cutting child marriage prevalence from one in five to one in seven within five years. Africa can lead the way to that target, but only if we treat every girl’s classroom as the place where her childhood is protected. Any girl-child should be a student, not a bride. She should learn, then lead. The post “A Girl Who Learns Is a Girl Who Is Not a Bride” – Obiageli “Oby” Ezekwesili appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Aspira Nigeria Celebrates Three Wins at Marketing Edge Awards 2026
item.description: Aspira Nigeria Limited, manufacturer of Viva detergent, Viva Dishwashing Liquid, and Oracare Toothpaste, among other household-care brands, has received three recognitions at the 2026 Marketing Edge Awards, with its brands recognised across the liquid dishwash, bar soap and detergent categories. The company received the Outstanding Liquid Dishwash Brand of the Year award, while Viva Multipurpose Soap was named Outstanding Bar Soap Brand of the Year. Aspira also received the Outstanding Detergent Brand of the Decade award, recognising its longstanding presence in Nigeria’s detergent category. The awards ceremony was held on Friday, September 25, at Ten Degrees Event Hall, Billings Way, Oregun, Ikeja, bringing together brands, marketing professionals and stakeholders from across Nigeria’s marketing, advertising and communications industry. The Marketing Edge Awards recognise brands and professionals across the marketing and communications sector, with categories covering different aspects of brand building, consumer engagement and industry performance. For Aspira, the three recognitions span different areas of its household-care portfolio. The liquid dishwash and bar soap awards recognise its presence in two competitive household categories, while the Detergent Brand of the Decade award acknowledges the longer-term journey of its detergent business. Speaking on the recognitions, Barbara Onianwah, Head of Marketing, Aspira Nigeria Limited, said the awards acknowledged the consistency required to build and sustain brands in a competitive market. “These recognitions are meaningful because they reflect the consistency and work that go into building brands that remain relevant to consumers. We are pleased that the awards recognise different areas of our portfolio, as well as the longer journey of our detergent business. For us, it is an encouragement to continue listening to consumers, learning from the market and evolving our approach,” she said. The recognitions come as brands in Nigeria’s fast-moving consumer goods sector continue to respond to changing consumer preferences and increased competition across household-care categories. With the three awards spanning liquid dishwash, bar soap and detergent, Aspira’s recognition at the 2026 Marketing Edge Awards reflects its presence across multiple segments of the household-care market, while the decade award highlights the longer history of its detergent business. The Marketing Edge Awards provided an opportunity for brands and industry professionals to come together and celebrate notable work and achievements within Nigeria’s marketing and communications landscape. item.title: Some of Ayra Starr’s Iconic Live Performances
item.description: Ayra Starr performing at the NFL Halftime Show in London There are not many great live performers in music. Some artists are very good but are only comfortable in the studio, which is understandable because music, like writing, is a solitary work and would require extra force or pull to stand before an audience and perform. But there are also great live performers who, despite how good they are in the studio, are also comfortable bringing the music to a live audience. There is something special about that, watching an artist bring their music to life on stage. The vocals, the choreography, the stage presence, the connection with the audience — sometimes, a live performance makes you appreciate a song in an entirely new way. There aren’t many with the artistry in Afrobeats. But Ayra Starr has made herself one of Afrobeats’ most exciting performers, and has constantly used the stage as another place to show the world her sability . From commanding festival stages and performing at major international music events to delivering memorable renditions of her biggest hits, Ayra Starr has continued to prove that her talent extends beyond the recording studio. She knows how to bring her music, personality, and energy together in a way that keeps audiences watching. As her global profile continues to grow, with her recent 2026 NFL Halftime International Games performance in London, we’re looking back at some of Ayra Starr’s most iconic live performances: Ayra Starr – Rush | Glastonbury 2024 Ayra Starr & ZAYN – Heaven Baby (Live Performance @ All Points East 2026) Ayra Starr – Rush (Live Performance in Paris) Ayra Starr – Live at Global Citizen Festival 2025 (Full Performance) Ayra Starr | Live – Les Ardentes 2024 Ayra Starr Lights Up Eden Park with “Commas” | Coldplay’s Music of the Spheres Tour (Auckland) The post Some of Ayra Starr’s Iconic Live Performances appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Watch Ayra Starr’s 2026 NFL Halftime Performance!
item.description: Ayra Starr performing at the NFL Halftime Show in London Since Ayra Starr emerged into the music scene with her debut EP, “Ayra Starr”, in 2021, she has gone on to break and set many records. But of all the records broken and set, none might top the feeling of being the first African artist to headline an NFL International Games Halftime Show. On Sunday, the 11th of October, 2026, at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London, Ayra Starr made the dream a reality. Before 61,322 people in attendance, Ayra dazzled on stage and not only made herself proud, but also made her country and language proud. She opened her performance with an emotional performance of “H eaven Baby”, her fan-favourite song featuring Zayn Malik , followed by a soulful performance of her Grammy-nominated song, “Rush.” She concluded the performance with songs from her latest album, “Starrgirl”, such as “D angerous,” “H ot Body,” and “Ms Paper.” Ayra Starr performing at the NFL Halftime Show in London Watch the full performance below: The post Watch Ayra Starr’s 2026 NFL Halftime Performance! appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: iPhone 18 Pro Max review: Apple’s biggest, heaviest and longest-lasting superphone
item.description: A giant screen, big battery, rapid chip and top cameras push the great iPhone 18 Pro to the max with a price tag to match Apple’s largest Pro iPhone gets its biggest battery upgrade yet to make it a true two-day phone with new Siri AI and a variable aperture camera. The iPhone 18 Pro Max is the supersized sibling of the regular 18 Pro and, though it is no longer Apple’s most expensive phone thanks to the £2,000 iPhone Duo , it has a similarly large price tag to match costing from £1,299 (€1,599/$1,299/A$2,299). item.title: How to Watch Ayra Starr’s NFL Halftime Performance: Kick-Off Time and Where to Stream
item.description: Ayra Starr at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium ahead of her historic NFL halftime show performance in London. Ayra Starr is taking Afrobeats to the football field, and this time, we’re talking American football! The Nigerian superstar is set to make history as the first African artiste to headline an NFL international halftime show when she performs at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London on Sunday, 11 October 2026. And with the Philadelphia Eagles facing the Jacksonville Jaguars, football fans will have a little extra entertainment to look forward to during the break. For Ayra, whose music has travelled from Nigeria to audiences around the world, this is another exciting addition to her growing list of international performances. This time, she’ll be introducing even more sports fans to her music, with songs from her Starrgirl project making their way to one of the NFL’s biggest international platforms. And what can fans expect to hear? Well, we’re hoping some of our favourites make the setlist. Perhaps “ Hot Body ” and “ Tornado ”, or even “ Heaven Baby ”, her collaboration with ZAYN . Nothing has been confirmed about the songs she’ll perform, but we’re already curious to see what she has planned for the halftime show. Ayra Starr speaking at the NFL London Games press conference ahead of her performance. If you’re planning to watch from Nigeria, here’s what you need to know. The Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars game is scheduled to kick off at 2:30 PM British Summer Time (BST), which is 2:30 PM West Africa Time (WAT). In the UK, viewers can catch the game on ITV1 and Sky Sports NFL, while fans in Nigeria and other supported regions can watch through DAZN’s NFL Game Pass. Viewers in the United States can tune in on FOX. The halftime performance will take place during the match, so keep an eye on the game if you don’t want to miss Ayra’s set. From performing her songs on music stages to preparing for an NFL halftime show in London, Ayra Starr keeps finding new audiences for her music. And for Nigerian fans watching from home, there’s something particularly exciting about seeing one of our own take the stage at an international sporting event of this scale. *** Photo Credit: Ayra Starr/Instagram The post How to Watch Ayra Starr’s NFL Halftime Performance: Kick-Off Time and Where to Stream appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: Chinazaekpere Chukwu’s First Feature Film Her Daughters’ Mother Heads to London for Film Africa 2026
item.description: Ejovwoke Obas Olikuntuyi delivers a powerful performance as Ejiro in Her Daughters’ Mother Nollywood is having an incredible global moment, and we couldn’t be prouder to cheer on our home-grown talents as they take their stories to the world. Filmmaker Chinazaekpere Chukwu is making her feature directorial debut with Her Daughters’ Mother , and the poignant Nigerian drama has been officially selected to screen at Film Africa 2026. Scheduled for an October 28 screening at the newly launched EbonyLife Place London, the 110-minute feature explores womanhood, sacrifice, and the enduring bond between mothers and daughters. Speaking on the emotional backbone of the project, Chinazaekpere Chukwu shared: It’s intended to feel like a juxtaposition of ‘ The Joys of Motherhood ‘ by Buchi Emecheta and ‘ Stay With M e’ by Ayọ̀bámi Adébáyọ̀ . It reaches deep into the rights of women, how their lives are decided for them until the end, first by their families/spouses and finally by their kids. Her Daughters’ Mother highlights the quiet resilience and domestic weight carried by women across generations. Set against the rich cultural backdrop of Benin and filmed early this year in English, Pidgin, Urhobo, and Bini, the story follows 33-year-old Ejiro (played by Ejovwoke Obas Olikuntuyi ). After being married off at the tender age of 16, Ejiro returns home in her thirties as a widowed mother of two daughters, determined to secure a brighter future for them. Faced with limited options, she enters a second marriage with Osato ( Philip Asaya ), a lorry driver who promises security and education for her girls in exchange for a male heir. However, when Ejiro struggles to fulfill his demands, Osato’s entitlement turns her life into a nightmare, leaving her longing for the freedom she last felt as a child. Meanwhile, her eldest daughter Ejaita ( Osas Okonyon ), a bright 16-year-old dreaming of becoming a doctor, struggles against her mother’s overprotectiveness, unaware of the immense sacrifices being made on her behalf. Osas Okonyon stars as Ejaita, a bright teenager whose ambitious dreams clash with her mother’s protective sacrifices. The film boasts an exceptional cast, including Najite Dede and Adeoluwa Akintoba . Behind the scenes, Chukwu —who wrote the screenplay alongside Sunday Melvin Iwinosa from a story by Efosa Ogbomo —collaborated with cinematographer Yinka Adegoke , executive producer and co-producer Efosa Ogbomo , and story consultant and editor Joshua Tsotso . Adeoluwa Akintoba in a scene from Her Daughters’ Mother, exploring youth and ambition. Chukwu’s transition to feature filmmaking follows her award-winning streak at the EbonyLife Creative Academy, where she graduated with the Best Director award for A Psalm for Abigail, as well as her standout short film Ti e Nbo , which screened in the Shorts category at AFRIFF in 2023. item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: BBNaija Season 11’s Final Five Talked Boldness, Authenticity & What Comes Next With Guinness
item.description: BBNaija Season 11 finalists Sheba, Aikou, and winner Temi Nkem reflect on living boldly during their Guinness post-eviction sit-down. As intense as Big Brother Naija can get, nothing quite compares to the tension of finale night! Who will make it into the final five? Who will be among the last three standing? And when Ebuka Obi – Uchendu finally announces the first runner-up, whose name will he call as the winner? Now, imagine being one of the housemates standing on that stage, waiting to hear your name. The suspense alone! But making it that far is a story of its own. The final ten housemates had spent weeks navigating friendships, disagreements, nominations, wagers and all the surprises Biggie had waiting for them. Getting into the Top 10 meant they had played the game boldly, made decisions along the way and found ways to keep going, even when things didn’t work out as planned. And when the season finally wrapped up, we had a few questions for the last five standing. With Guinness, a brand that celebrates boldness and authenticity, powering our BBNaija Season 11 finale post-eviction interviews, we sat down with winner Temi Nkem and fellow finalists Aikou, Sheba, Tram and Bluethopia to talk about their time in Biggie’s house, the choices they made, the courage it took to stay true to themselves and what comes next. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) Of course, we wanted to know how they managed to remain grounded while living with a houseful of distinct personalities under 24/7 camera surveillance. There were friendships to navigate, difficult decisions to make and times when speaking up or standing your ground took courage. So, what did living boldly look like for each of them? For Temi Nkem, the conversation explored the instincts and decisions that helped her navigate the competition all the way to the winning spot. Aikou, Sheba, Tram and Bluethopia also reflected on their individual journeys, how they approached the game and what they learnt about themselves along the way. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) And now that the cameras are off and life outside Biggie’s house has begun, what’s next? The finalists shared their plans for the future, the opportunities they’re looking forward to and how they hope to carry that same boldness into their next chapters. Powered by Guinness , these conversations gave us another chance to hear from the housemates after the competition, this time with the pressure of nominations and evictions behind them. After weeks of watching their stories unfold inside the house, we got to hear them tell those stories in their own words. item.title: From Kitchen Bowls to Task Battles: How Checkers Custard Powered BBNaija Season 11
item.description: Big Brother Naija Season 11 winner Temi Nkem poses with a jar of Checkers Custard Vanilla Flavour. Photo Credit: Checkers Custard/Instagram If there is one thing about life in Biggie’s house, it is that there is always something going on. Between the housemates’ conversations, their daily routines, the strategies and the tasks that kept them on their toes, BBNaija Season 11 had no shortage of activity. And through it all, Checkers Custard was right there, serving the housemates creamy custard throughout the show. Because even when you are busy navigating life with 23 other people, there is always room for a comforting bowl of custard! From breakfast before the day’s activities to kitchen catch-ups with fellow housemates, Checkers Custard was part of the everyday experience inside the house. Those kitchen visits were also a chance to catch up, share a laugh and take a breather before the next task or surprise from Biggie. With so much happening under one roof, having something creamy to enjoy was a welcome addition to the routine. And speaking of tasks, Checkers Custard had something special in store for the housemates, too. The Checkers Custard Task called for mental agility, physical endurance and teamwork, giving the housemates a chance to put their skills to the test. With Head of House Tram stepping in as Game Master, the house was split into two teams: Team Creamy and Team Tasty. Now, it was time to see which side could pull together and claim the win. Checkers Custard got the housemates running @CheckersCustard #BNxBBNaija11 #BBNaijaS11 #BBNaija #BBNaijaxCheckersCustard https://t.co/geVfgwtZpz — BellaNaija (@bellanaija) September 12, 2026 First, the housemates had to tackle custom obstacle courses, scrambling to collect branded jars along the way. Then came fast-paced physical relays, followed by blindfolded directional challenges that required them to listen carefully and trust their teammates’ instructions. Imagine trying to find your way around without being able to see, while someone else directs your every move! You would need a good deal of patience, communication and teamwork to make it through. Both teams competed for points across the different games, and there was plenty to play for. When the scores were finally counted, Team Creamy came out on top with 140 points, beating Team Tasty to claim the win. Flora , Keivo , Aikou , Araga , Barry , Bells and Bluetopia made up the winning team, with Tram taking on the role of Game Master. That is a win worth celebrating. In the second task, they must select representatives who must pick a Checkers Custard jar as fast as possible when they hear the buzzer. They will be given tasks like ‘touch your ear, touch your toes’ before the buzzer sound. If they pick the jar before the buzzer, they lose a point. The team with the most jar wins. #BNxBBNaija11 #BBNaijaS11 #BBNaija #BBNaijaxCheckersCustard — BellaNaija (@bellanaija) September 12, 2026 From keeping the housemates supplied with creamy cust

item.title: Ships, Gbas Gbos & Chinchin! Minimie Joined the BBNaija Season 11 Fun
item.description: Aikou, Temi Nkem, and Barry secure their places among the Big Brother Naija Season 11 Top 10 finalists Have you been keeping up with BBNaija Season 11? Because between the ships that sailed, the ones that sank, the gbas gbos, the strategic gambits, the twists nobody saw coming and those shaking eviction nights, 24 housemates gave us a whole lot to discuss. And then there was the big question: who would walk away with the crown? After 70 days in Biggie’s house, Temi Nkem emerged as the winner, bringing the season to a close after weeks of entertainment, surprises and conversations that kept BNers talking. Temi Nkem is officially crowned the winner of Big Brother Naija Season 11. Throughout the season, BellaNaija’s weekly recaps on our website kept readers up to date with the latest happenings, while FunTime with Coco brought the conversation to our social media platforms. Our witty AI character had her own commentary on the housemates and their antics, giving BNers another reason to laugh, react and feel as though they were right there in Biggie’s house with the housemates. Between the weekly recaps and Coco’s cheeky takes, there was always another bit of gist to get into. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) Now, let’s talk snacks. Because you cannot be expected to follow a ship’s entire journey, debate a housemate’s strategy and survive a shaking eviction without something to munch on. Minimie Chinchin was the go-to snack for the housemates and viewers at home, ready for those stretches of top-notch entertainment when you simply had to know what happened next. Watching with friends? Grab a snack. Catching up on the latest gist? Grab a snack. Settling in to see how the season would unfold? You get the idea. When the housemates heard it’s @MinimieNigeria, they could not contain their joy. They are used to the taste of fun that Minimie brings. The brief is in! Ladies and gentlemen, it’s time @MinimieNigeria’s task in BBNaija house! Housemates will be grouped into four groups! #MinimieXBBNaija #TasteTheFunWithMinimie #MinimieXBellaNaija #BBNaija #BNxBBNaija11 — BellaNaija (@bellanaija) August 29, 2026 As an associate sponsor of BBNaija Season 11, Minimie Chinchin also brought a challenge to the house, taking the fun from the snack break to the arena. The Minimie Chinchin Challenge featured three rounds designed to test the housemates’ speed, coordination, strategy and teamwork. It was a chance for the teams to put their skills to work, and they had to do more than cheer one another on from the sidelines. The challenge opened with “Catch the Flavours,” an obstacle course that required housemates to cross balance beams and collect branded tokens before time ran out. In “Complete the Word,” teams worked with giant puzzle pieces to solve the challenge together. Watching with friends? Grab a snack. Catching up on the latest gist? Grab a snack. Settling in to see how the season would unfold? You get the idea. When the housemates heard it’s @MinimieNigeria, they could not contain their joy. They are used to the taste of fun that Minimie brings. The brief is in! Ladies and gentlemen, it’s time @MinimieNigeria’s task in BBNaija house! Housemates will be grouped into four groups! #MinimieXBBNaija #TasteTheFunWithMinimie #MinimieXBellaNaija #BBNaija #BNxBBNaija11 — BellaNaija (@bellanaija) August 29, 2026 As an associate sponsor of BBNaija Season 11, Minimie Chinchin also brought a challenge to the house, taking the fun from the snack break to the arena. The Minimie Chinchin Challenge featured three rounds designed to test the housemates’ speed, coordination, strategy and teamwork. It was a chance for the teams to put their skills to work, and they had to do more than cheer one another on from the sidelines. The challenge opened with “Catch the Flavours,” an obstacle course that required housemates to cross balance beams and collect branded tokens before time ran out. In “Complete the Word,” teams worked with giant puzzle pieces to solve the challenge together. The final round, “The Junk Dash,” introduced a blindfolded relay, with housemates depending on their teammates’ directions to navigate obstacles. Each round came with its own demands, from keeping their balance to communicating clearly when they could not see where they were going. And the winners of the @MinimieNigeria task are Team Spicy Rebel with 1000 points. Congratulations to Flora, Gerard, Barry, Sultex and the game master, Chimsom Chuka. @MinimieNigeria #MinimieXBBNaija #TasteTheFunWithMinimie #MinimieXBellaNaija #BBNaija #BNxBBNaija11 https://t.co/ERFS8vzFrv — BellaNaija (@bellanaija) August 29, 2026 After the three rounds, Team Spicy Rebel came out on top. Flora, Barry, Gerard and Sultex, alongside Game Master Chimsom Chuka, secured the victory and earned the bragging rights that came with winning the challenge. The ships may have sailed or sunk, the gambits may have played out, and the evictions may have shaken up the house, but the fun with Minimie Chinchin never does. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: Uganda, We’re Coming! BellaNaija Heads to ADCCE 2026 in Kampala
item.description: Funmilola Sanya and Dorcas Anya head to Kampala for the Africa Destination Celebrations Conference & Expo (ADCCE 2026) to cover the latest in African celebration tourism for BellaNaija. Hi BNers, we’re heading to Uganda! From October 12th to 17th, 2026, BellaNaija’s Funmilola Sanya and Dorcas Anya will be in Kampala for the Africa Destination Celebrations Conference & Expo (ADCCE 2026). With the theme “ Africa Unveils Events in the Wild ,” ADCCE 2026 brings together wedding and event professionals, tourism stakeholders, hospitality executives, creatives, cultural curators, and industry leaders to explore Africa’s potential as the Celebration Capital of the World. The conference and expo will take place on 12th and 13th October 2026 at the Speke Resort Munyonyo Convention Centre in Kampala, Uganda, followed by destination experiences and familiarisation tours from October 14th to 17th. The gathering aims to showcase Africa’s rich cultural heritage, breathtaking landscapes, unique destinations, and world-class hospitality while creating opportunities for collaboration, investment, and growth across the continent’s celebration and tourism industries. Despite Africa’s incredible destinations and creative talent, the continent remains underrepresented in the global destination wedding and celebration tourism market. ADCCE seeks to change that narrative by connecting African destinations and businesses with international industry professionals and creating greater visibility for the continent’s offerings. For BellaNaija, this is an opportunity to experience Uganda, connect with industry leaders, and discover the people, places, and experiences shaping the future of African celebrations. We’ll be bringing you along for the journey, sharing highlights from the conference, destination experiences, and the memorable moments that make Africa such a special place to celebrate. Stay connected with us on BellaNaija’s social media pages and follow the conversation using #ADCCE2026, #UnveilingDestinationAfrica, #BNTravels. Uganda, we’ll see you soon! The post Uganda, We’re Coming! BellaNaija Heads to ADCCE 2026 in Kampala appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Leo Stan Ekeh Foundation Partners with Nigeria Computer Society to Support 1,000 Tech Scholars Through Mentorship
item.description: The Leo Stan Ekeh Foundation ( LSEF ) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Nigeria Computer Society ( NCS ) to provide mentorship, technical training and real-world technology experience to the Nigerian whiz kids under the Foundation’s technology scholarship initiative. The 1000 scholarship scheme, which was first announced by Africa’s foremost technology entrepreneur and Chairman of Zinox Group , Leo Stan Ekeh , is designed to empower indigent but exceptionally gifted Nigerian students to study Computer Science and other technology-related disciplines in federal and state universities, as well as polytechnics, across the country. The scholarship reflects Dr. Ekeh’s philosophy of “one family, one tech-empowered person” and will support 1,000 students selected from all 36 states of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory, irrespective of ethnic background. From their first year through graduation, beneficiaries will receive world-class technology training, skills development and monthly financial support. Each scholar will also have a dedicated mentor to provide guidance throughout their academic journey. Under the MoU, the NCS will provide technical support and practical learning through experienced and certified technology professionals. The programme will blend academic learning with real-world exposure, helping beneficiaries build technical competence, problem-solving skills and the confidence to apply their knowledge beyond the classroom. According to the Director of LSEF, Dr. George Emetuche , the programme will feature boot camps each semester, creating opportunities for students to learn beyond the classroom and gain practical experience. The objective, he explained, is to prepare beneficiaries not merely to graduate, but to become capable technology professionals who can solve real-world problems. Speaking at the ceremony, NCS President, Professor Muhammed Siraju Aliyu , described Dr. Leo Stan Ekeh as a nationalist who has consistently supported initiatives that create opportunities for Nigerians who may otherwise lack access. He noted that Dr. Ekeh’s relationship with the NCS predates the scholarship initiative and has contributed to the advancement of technology and human capital development. He also highlighted Dr. Ekeh’s technology innovation programmes, which identify young people with ideas, support them in developing their concepts and create opportunities for them to pitch to potential investors. Professor Aliyu expressed appreciation for Dr. Ekeh’s contributions to the NCS and reaffirmed the Society’s commitment to initiatives that support national growth and development. Representing the Zinox Group, Executive Director, Human Resources, Mrs. Chioma Nwoke , assured the Foundation and the NCS of the Group’s continued support for the initiative, cohort after cohort. Beyond the scholarship, the programme represents a long-term investment in Nigeria’s human capital. By helping 1,000 gifted young Nigerians

item.title: Watch Asake Trade Big Scenes for Studio Sessions in His “Oba” Music Video
item.description: Asake leans into his royal theme and signature high-steeze style, reflecting the confidence behind his hit track Oba. Photo Credit: Mr Money/Instagram Asake is keeping his foot firmly on the pedal, delivering fresh visuals for “ Oba ” from his latest project M$NEY . Directed by Director Buise, the newly released music video moves away from typical high-energy street setups to take fans directly inside the intimate, creative atmosphere of a late-night recording session. At its core, “Oba”—which translates to King in Yoruba—is a high-steeze anthem centred on royal status, relentless hustle, and staying grounded. Across the track, Asake leans into his “Mister Money” persona, blending Yoruba cultural references with reflections on his unstoppable work ethic. He balances bragging rights about his dominant position in the industry with street wisdom and gratitude, reminding listeners to remain vigilant and humble even as international success rolls in. On set for his Oba music video, Asake highlights his signature high-steeze look with a textured jacket and luxury travel accessories. Photo Credit: Mr Money/Instagram The visual brings this context to life, opening with a bass player laying down a rhythmic groove in a dimly lit studio before panning to Asake seated in the vocal booth. Clad in a green tracksuit over a white tank top, accessorised with thick gold chains, rings, and sunglasses, the YBNL star records his lines while surrounded by producers, engineers, and backing vocalists. The clip blends performance shots with real-time studio mechanics, showing engineers fine-tuning mixing boards, vocalists harmonising at the microphone, and producers triggering beats. Produced by long-time collaborator Magicsticks, “Oba” combines Asake’s signature log-drum rhythms with choir-backed harmonies. Rather than relying on large dance ensembles or cinematic storylines, the visual focuses on the pure craftsmanship behind the music, giving audiences a fly-on-the-wall perspective of how the hit came together in the studio. item.title: Sliding Doors meets Biff’s Almanac: City saga stirs up a world of alternate histories | Max Rushden
item.description: Even New Romantics have a view but this long story will not be cut short amid endless hypotheticals and split narratives It’s Wednesday afternoon (UK time) and I find myself interviewing Tony Hadley on TalkSport about his upcoming big band tour. We play a bit of Spandau Ballet, chat about the classics and his career – hanging out with Frank Sinatra and Tony Bennett. In as much as you can deduce in a 10-minute chat on Zoom, Tony seems like an absolute gent. We do always try to bring it back to sport – Tony is an Arsenal fan, there’s a bit of Arteta, Leeds at the weekend. Tony brings up Billy Bremner and suggests that my co-host Charlie Baker and I are too young to remember him playing. We are, and how wonderful to be called young. Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. Continue reading...

item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Lionel Messi’s Argentina career turned football into a sacred mystery
item.description: Jorge Messi wanted his country to fall in love with his son. That ambition was fulfilled during a brilliant international career that ended this week “What Argentina is doing in this World Cup is of a sacred order,” Brazilian writer Milly Lacombe posted at the height of the tide of anti-Argentinian sentiment during this year’s tournament. She was exploring the contradiction she felt around her support of Lionel Messi: “a player who is a God and a man who shakes Trump’s hand”. Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. How is it possible that Messi was not speaking out against the racist incidents we all saw around the Argentina team , she asked. “That’s why it hurts so much to see someone with Messi’s power choosing to make himself small,” she wrote. Continue reading...

item.title: OpenAI’s Jason Kwon gave even-toned, reassuring answers to the Australian government. Did … ChatGPT write this?
item.description: Kwon’s answers were provided in a helpful, quiet and calm manner, but his mea culpa left the audience not much the wiser Open AI’s Jason Kwon flew 15 hours from San Francisco to Sydney to give the company’s first in-person mea culpa after it admitted – in an unsigned email, to a public departmental inbox – that one of its AI agents had accessed a Services Australia website without authorisation and grabbed data related to Medicare. Kwon – polite, friendly, even-toned – got through a potentially dicey parliamentary committee hearing unscathed, promising to do better and pledging assistance to Australia. No missteps, no viral moments, just delivering his answers helpfully, in a quiet and calm manner, sympathising with the questioner and the point they were making. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Mac mini M6 review: truly mighty but now more pricey
item.description: Apple’s cheapest desktop computer is no longer a bargain but its newest, fastest chip makes it a pocket powerhouse Apple’s latest Mac mini brings real speed and power for far more than everyday tasks in a practically pocketable form you can fit almost anywhere. The impressive new desktop machine is the first to receive an update to Apple’s latest M6 chip while remaining smaller than a headphones box. It is the cheapest computer Apple sells with an M-series chip, but like every other memory-containing piece of electronics, it has been hit by RAMageddon , driving up the starting price to £899 (€1,049/$899/A$1,449) from the £599 or equivalent of its M4 predecessor. Continue reading...

item.title: Superbubble in the Large Magellanic Cloud
item.description: N44 is a complex nebula filled with glowing hydrogen gas, dark lanes of dust, massive stars, and many populations of stars of different ages. One of its most distinctive features, however, is the dark, starry gap called a “superbubble,” visible in this Hubble Space Telescope image in the upper central region.

item.title: Lunar Occultation of Venus
item.description: On Wednesday, June 17, skywatchers across the United States—and parts of Canada—enjoyed a rare event: a daytime lunar occultation of Venus. A lunar occultation occurs when the Moon moves directly in front of another celestial object from our viewpoint on Earth, briefly hiding it from sight.

item.title: August Lunar Eclipse Rises Over Louisiana
item.description: A lunar eclipse is visible over southern Louisiana. The lunar eclipse was visible throughout much of North and South America and part of Europe and Africa between Aug. 27-28. The Full Moon slipped through Earth’s shadow on Aug. 27, continuing into Aug. 28 for some parts of the world, resulting in the lunar eclipse. At maximum eclipse, the Moon takes on a dramatic dark, ruddy or coppery tint along the covered edge. New Orleans is home to NASA’s Michoud Assembly Facility, where stages for NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket and structures for Orion spacecraft are produced for the Artemis missions.

item.title: Artemis III RS-25 Engine Processing: #3 Lift

item.title: Colorful Collage of Tarantula Nebula
item.description: Like a collage made of layered sheets of colored cellophane, a vibrant new image layers observations of a famous star-forming nebula from NASA space telescopes. The resulting cosmic “craft” reveals new details about the star formation region known as 30 Doradus, or the Tarantula Nebula.

item.title: Microsoft Surface Laptop 8 review: a quality PC whose trackpad taps you back
item.description: Snappy performance, long battery life, great keyboard and excellent new haptic touchpad make the best of Windows 11 Microsoft’s Surface laptop for consumers is back, faster and with longer battery life and a hefty price increase because of the high cost of memory and chips. The Surface Laptop 8 is a straight replacement for the seventh edition from 2024, which was the first of Microsoft’s new generation of ARM-based, Qualcomm-powered PCs designed to better rival Apple’s MacBook Air and other thin and light machines. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...
